units.leftText: Now King David was old and well along in years, and though they covered him with blankets, he could not keep warm.
units.rightText: Now king David was old and stricken in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he gat no heat.

units.leftText: So his servants said to him, “Let us search for a young virgin for our lord the king, to attend to him and care for him and lie by his side to keep him warm.”
units.rightText: Wherefore his servants said unto him, Let there be sought for my lord the king a young virgin: and let her stand before the king, and cherish him; and let her lie in thy bosom, that my lord the king may get heat.

units.leftText: Then they searched throughout Israel for a beautiful girl, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.
units.rightText: So they sought for a fair damsel throughout all the borders of Israel, and found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king.

units.leftText: The girl was unsurpassed in beauty; she cared for the king and served him, but he had no relations with her. Adonijah Usurps the Kingdom
units.rightText: And the damsel was very fair; and she cherished the king, and ministered to him; but the king knew her not.

units.leftText: At that time Adonijah, David’s son by Haggith, began to exalt himself, saying, “I will be king!” And he acquired chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run ahead of him.
units.rightText: Then Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, I will be king: and he prepared him chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.

units.leftText: (His father had never once reprimanded him by saying, “Why do you act this way?” Adonijah was also very handsome, born next after Absalom.)
units.rightText: And his father had not displeased him at any time in saying, Why hast thou done so? and he was also a very goodly man; and he was born after Absalom.

units.leftText: So Adonijah conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, who supported him.
units.rightText: And he conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah, and with Abiathar the priest: and they following Adonijah helped him.

units.leftText: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David’s mighty men would not join Adonijah.
units.rightText: But Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and Nathan the prophet, and Shimei, and Rei, and the mighty men that belonged to David, were not with Adonijah.

units.leftText: And Adonijah sacrificed sheep, oxen, and fattened calves near the stone of Zoheleth, which is next to En-rogel. He invited all his royal brothers and all the men of Judah who were servants of the king.
units.rightText: And Adonijah slew sheep and oxen and fatlings by the stone of Zoheleth, which is beside En-rogel; and he called all his brethren, the king’s sons, and all the men of Judah, the king’s servants:
leftNotes: 1:9 Or the Serpent’s Stone

units.leftText: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, or his brother Solomon. Nathan and Bathsheba before David
units.rightText: but Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, and the mighty men, and Solomon his brother, he called not.

units.leftText: Then Nathan said to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, “Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David does not know it?
units.rightText: Then Nathan spake unto Bath-sheba the mother of Solomon, saying, Hast thou not heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith doth reign, and David our lord knoweth it not?

units.leftText: Now please, come and let me advise you. Save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.
units.rightText: Now therefore come, let me, I pray thee, give thee counsel, that thou mayest save thine own life, and the life of thy son Solomon.

units.leftText: Go at once to King David and say, ‘My lord the king, did you not swear to your maidservant, “Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne”? Why then has Adonijah become king?’
units.rightText: Go and get thee in unto king David, and say unto him, Didst not thou, my lord, O king, swear unto thy handmaid, saying, Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne? why then doth Adonijah reign?

units.leftText: Then, while you are still there speaking with the king, I will come in after you and confirm your words.”
units.rightText: Behold, while thou yet talkest there with the king, I also will come in after thee, and confirm thy words.

units.leftText: So Bathsheba went to see the king in his bedroom. Since the king was very old, Abishag the Shunammite was serving him.
units.rightText: And Bath-sheba went in unto the king into the chamber: and the king was very old; and Abishag the Shunammite was ministering unto the king.

units.leftText: And Bathsheba bowed down in homage to the king, who asked, “What is your desire?”
units.rightText: And Bath-sheba bowed, and did obeisance unto the king. And the king said, What wouldest thou?

units.leftText: “My lord,” she replied, “you yourself swore to your maidservant by the LORD your God: ‘Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne.’
units.rightText: And she said unto him, My lord, thou swarest by Jehovah thy God unto thy handmaid, saying, Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne.

units.leftText: But now, behold, Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, do not know it.
units.rightText: And now, behold, Adonijah reigneth; and thou, my lord the king, knowest it not:

units.leftText: And he has sacrificed an abundance of oxen, fattened calves, and sheep, and has invited all the other sons of the king, as well as Abiathar the priest and Joab the commander of the army. But he has not invited your servant Solomon.
units.rightText: and he hath slain oxen and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and hath called all the sons of the king, and Abiathar the priest, and Joab the captain of the host; but Solomon thy servant hath he not called.

units.leftText: And as for you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are upon you to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
units.rightText: And thou, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are upon thee, that thou shouldest tell them who shall sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.

units.leftText: Otherwise, when my lord the king rests with his fathers, I and my son Solomon will be counted as criminals.”
units.rightText: Otherwise it will come to pass, when my lord the king shall sleep with his fathers, that I and my son Solomon shall be counted offenders.

units.leftText: And just then, while Bathsheba was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.
units.rightText: And, lo, while she yet talked with the king, Nathan the prophet came in.

units.leftText: So the king was told, “Nathan the prophet is here.” And Nathan went in and bowed facedown before the king.
units.rightText: And they told the king, saying, Behold, Nathan the prophet. And when he was come in before the king, he bowed himself before the king with his face to the ground.

units.leftText: “My lord the king,” said Nathan, “did you say, ‘Adonijah will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne’?
units.rightText: And Nathan said, My lord, O king, hast thou said, Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne?

units.leftText: For today he has gone down and sacrificed an abundance of oxen, fattened calves, and sheep, and has invited all the sons of the king, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest. And behold, they are eating and drinking before him, saying, ‘Long live King Adonijah!’
units.rightText: For he is gone down this day, and hath slain oxen and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and hath called all the king’s sons, and the captains of the host, and Abiathar the priest; and, behold, they are eating and drinking before him, and say, Long live king Adonijah.
leftNotes: 1:25 Hebrew; LXX Joab the commander

units.leftText: But me your servant he has not invited, nor Zadok the priest, nor Benaiah son of Jehoiada, nor your servant Solomon.
units.rightText: But me, even me thy servant, and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and thy servant Solomon, hath he not called.

units.leftText: Has my lord the king let this happen without informing your servant who should sit on the throne after my lord the king?” David Renews His Oath to Bathsheba
units.rightText: Is this thing done by my lord the king, and thou hast not showed unto thy servants who should sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?

units.leftText: Then King David said, “Call in Bathsheba for me.” So she came into the king’s presence and stood before him.
units.rightText: Then king David answered and said, Call to me Bath-sheba. And she came into the king’s presence, and stood before the king.

units.leftText: And the king swore an oath, saying, “As surely as the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from all distress,
units.rightText: And the king sware, and said, As Jehovah liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,

units.leftText: I will carry out this very day exactly what I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel: Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne in my place.”
units.rightText: verily as I sware unto thee by Jehovah, the God of Israel, saying, Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne in my stead; verily so will I do this day.

units.leftText: Bathsheba bowed facedown in homage to the king and said, “May my lord King David live forever!” Solomon Anointed King (1 Chronicles 29:21–25|1CH 29:21-25*)
units.rightText: Then Bath-sheba bowed with her face to the earth, and did obeisance to the king, and said, Let my lord king David live for ever.

units.leftText: Then King David said, “Call in for me Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada.” So they came before the king.
units.rightText: And king David said, Call to me Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada. And they came before the king.

units.leftText: “Take my servants with you,” said the king. “Set my son Solomon on my own mule and take him down to Gihon.
units.rightText: And the king said unto them, Take with you the servants of your lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride upon mine own mule, and bring him down to Gihon:

units.leftText: There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet are to anoint him king over Israel. You are to blow the ram’s horn and declare, ‘Long live King Solomon!’
units.rightText: and let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there king over Israel; and blow ye the trumpet, and say, Long live king Solomon.

units.leftText: Then you shall go up with him, and he is to come and sit on my throne and reign in my place. For I have appointed him ruler over Israel and Judah.”
units.rightText: Then ye shall come up after him, and he shall come and sit upon my throne; for he shall be king in my stead; and I have appointed him to be prince over Israel and over Judah.

units.leftText: “Amen,” replied Benaiah son of Jehoiada. “May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, so declare it.
units.rightText: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada answered the king, and said, Amen: Jehovah, the God of my lord the king, say so too.

units.leftText: Just as the LORD was with my lord the king, so may He be with Solomon and make his throne even greater than that of my lord King David.”
units.rightText: As Jehovah hath been with my lord the king, even so be he with Solomon, and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord king David.

units.leftText: Then Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, along with the Cherethites and Pelethites, went down and set Solomon on King David’s mule, and they escorted him to Gihon.
units.rightText: So Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, went down, and caused Solomon to ride upon king David’s mule, and brought him to Gihon.

units.leftText: Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tabernacle and anointed Solomon. Then they blew the ram’s horn, and all the people proclaimed, “Long live King Solomon!”
units.rightText: And Zadok the priest took the horn of oil out of the Tent, and anointed Solomon. And they blew the trumpet; and all the people said, Long live king Solomon.

units.leftText: All the people followed him, playing flutes and rejoicing with such a great joy that the earth was split by the sound. Adonijah Learns of Solomon’s Kingship
units.rightText: And all the people came up after him, and the people piped with pipes, and rejoiced with great joy, so that the earth rent with the sound of them.

units.leftText: Now Adonijah and all his guests were finishing their feast when they heard the sound of the ram’s horn. “Why is the city in such a loud uproar?” asked Joab.
units.rightText: And Adonijah and all the guests that were with him heard it as they had made an end of eating. And when Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he said, Wherefore is this noise of the city being in an uproar?

units.leftText: As he was speaking, suddenly Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest arrived. “Come in,” said Adonijah, “for you are a man of valor. You must be bringing good news.”
units.rightText: While he yet spake, behold, Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest came: and Adonijah said, Come in; for thou art a worthy man, and bringest good tidings.

units.leftText: “Not at all,” Jonathan replied. “Our lord King David has made Solomon king.
units.rightText: And Jonathan answered and said to Adonijah, Verily our lord king David hath made Solomon king:

units.leftText: And with Solomon, the king has sent Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, along with the Cherethites and Pelethites, and they have set him on the king’s mule.
units.rightText: and the king hath sent with him Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and they have caused him to ride upon the king’s mule;

units.leftText: Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king at Gihon, and they have gone up from there with rejoicing that rings out in the city. That is the noise you hear.
units.rightText: and Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king in Gihon; and they are come up from thence rejoicing, so that the city rang again. This is the noise that ye have heard.

units.leftText: Moreover, Solomon has taken his seat on the royal throne.
units.rightText: And also Solomon sitteth on the throne of the kingdom.

units.leftText: The king’s servants have also gone to congratulate our lord King David, saying, ‘May your God make the name of Solomon more famous than your own name, and may He make his throne greater than your throne.’
units.rightText: And moreover the king’s servants came to bless our lord king David, saying, Thy God make the name of Solomon better than thy name, and make his throne greater than thy throne: and the king bowed himself upon the bed.

units.leftText: saying, ‘Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel! Today He has provided one to sit on my throne, and my eyes have seen it.’”
units.rightText: And also thus said the king, Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Israel, who hath given one to sit on my throne this day, mine eyes even seeing it.
leftNotes: 1:48 LXX one of my offspring

units.leftText: At this, all the guests of Adonijah arose in terror and scattered.
units.rightText: And all the guests of Adonijah were afraid, and rose up, and went every man his way.

units.leftText: But Adonijah, in fear of Solomon, got up and went to take hold of the horns of the altar.
units.rightText: And Adonijah feared because of Solomon; and he arose, and went, and caught hold on the horns of the altar.

units.leftText: It was reported to Solomon: “Behold, Adonijah fears King Solomon, and he has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, ‘Let King Solomon first swear to me not to put his servant to the sword.’”
units.rightText: And it was told Solomon, saying, Behold, Adonijah feareth king Solomon; for, lo, he hath laid hold on the horns of the altar, saying, Let king Solomon swear unto me first that he will not slay his servant with the sword.

units.leftText: And Solomon replied, “If he is a man of character, not a single hair of his will fall to the ground. But if evil is found in him, he will die.”
units.rightText: And Solomon said, If he shall show himself a worthy man, there shall not a hair of him fall to the earth; but if wickedness be found in him, he shall die.

units.leftText: So King Solomon summoned Adonijah down from the altar, and he came and bowed down before King Solomon, who said to him, “Go to your home.”
units.rightText: So king Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar. And he came and did obeisance to king Solomon; and Solomon said unto him, Go to thy house.

units.leftText: As the time drew near for David to die, he charged his son Solomon,
units.rightText: Now the days of David drew nigh that he should die; and he charged Solomon his son, saying,

units.leftText: “I am about to go the way of all the earth. So be strong and prove yourself a man.
units.rightText: I am going the way of all the earth: be thou strong therefore, and show thyself a man;

units.leftText: And keep the charge of the LORD your God to walk in His ways and to keep His statutes, commandments, ordinances, and decrees, as written in the Law of Moses, so that you may prosper in all you do and wherever you turn,
units.rightText: and keep the charge of Jehovah thy God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his ordinances, and his testimonies, according to that which is written in the law of Moses, that thou mayest prosper in all that thou doest, and whithersoever thou turnest thyself;

units.leftText: and so that the LORD may fulfill His promise to me: ‘If your descendants take heed to walk faithfully before Me with all their heart and soul, you will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel.’
units.rightText: that Jehovah may establish his word which he spake concerning me, saying, If thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail thee (said he) a man on the throne of Israel.

units.leftText: Moreover, you know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me— what he did to Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, the two commanders of the armies of Israel. He killed them in peacetime to avenge the blood of war. He stained with the blood of war the belt around his waist and the sandals on his feet.
units.rightText: Moreover thou knowest also what Joab the son of Zeruiah did unto me, even what he did to the two captains of the hosts of Israel, unto Abner the son of Ner, and unto Amasa the son of Jether, whom he slew, and shed the blood of war in peace, and put the blood of war upon his girdle that was about his loins, and in his shoes that were on his feet.
leftNotes: 2:5 Jether is a variant of Ithra; also in verse 32; see 2 Samuel 17:25|2SA 17:25*.
2:5 Hebrew; LXX He stained with innocent blood the belt around my waist and the sandals on my feet.

units.leftText: So act according to your wisdom, and do not let his gray head go down to Sheol in peace.
units.rightText: Do therefore according to thy wisdom, and let not his hoar head go down to Sheol in peace.

units.leftText: But show loving devotion to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, because they stood by me when I fled from your brother Absalom.
units.rightText: But show kindness unto the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be of those that eat at thy table; for so they came to me when I fled from Absalom thy brother.
leftNotes: 2:7 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: Keep an eye on Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite from Bahurim who is with you. He called down bitter curses against me on the day I went to Mahanaim, but when he came down to meet me at the Jordan, I swore to him by the LORD: ‘I will never put you to the sword.’
units.rightText: And, behold, there is with thee Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite, of Bahurim, who cursed me with a grievous curse in the day when I went to Mahanaim; but he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I sware to him by Jehovah, saying, I will not put thee to death with the sword.

units.leftText: Now therefore, do not hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man. You know what you ought to do to him to bring his gray head down to Sheol in blood.” David’s Reign and Death (1 Chronicles 29:26–30|1CH 29:26-30*)
units.rightText: Now therefore hold him not guiltless, for thou art a wise man; and thou wilt know what thou oughtest to do unto him, and thou shalt bring his hoar head down to Sheol with blood.

units.leftText: Then David rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.
units.rightText: And David slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David.

units.leftText: The length of David’s reign over Israel was forty years — seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And the days that David reigned over Israel were forty years: seven years reigned he in Hebron, and thirty and three years reigned he in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: So Solomon sat on the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was firmly established. The Execution of Adonijah
units.rightText: And Solomon sat upon the throne of David his father; and his kingdom was established greatly.

units.leftText: Now Adonijah son of Haggith went to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, and she asked, “Do you come in peace?”
units.rightText: Then Adonijah the son of Haggith came to Bath-sheba the mother of Solomon. And she said, Comest thou peaceably? And he said, Peaceably.

units.leftText: Then he said, “I have something to tell you.” “Say it,” she answered.
units.rightText: He said moreover, I have somewhat to say unto thee. And she said, Say on.

units.leftText: “You know that the kingship was mine,” he said. “All Israel expected that I should reign, but the kingship has turned to my brother, for it has come to him from the LORD.
units.rightText: And he said, Thou knowest that the kingdom was mine, and that all Israel set their faces on me, that I should reign: howbeit the kingdom is turned about, and is become my brother’s; for it was his from Jehovah.

units.leftText: So now I have just one request of you; do not deny me.” “State your request,” she told him.
units.rightText: And now I ask one petition of thee; deny me not. And she said unto him, Say on.

units.leftText: Adonijah replied, “Please speak to King Solomon, since he will not turn you down. Let him give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife.”
units.rightText: And he said, Speak, I pray thee, unto Solomon the king (for he will not say thee nay), that he give me Abishag the Shunammite to wife.

units.leftText: “Very well,” Bathsheba replied. “I will speak to the king for you.”
units.rightText: And Bath-sheba said, Well; I will speak for thee unto the king.

units.leftText: So Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah. The king stood up to greet her, bowed to her, and sat down on his throne. Then the king had a throne brought for his mother, who sat down at his right hand.
units.rightText: Bath-sheba therefore went unto king Solomon, to speak unto him for Adonijah. And the king rose up to meet her, and bowed himself unto her, and sat down on his throne, and caused a throne to be set for the king’s mother; and she sat on his right hand.

units.leftText: “I have just one small request of you,” she said. “Do not deny me.” “Make your request, my mother,” the king replied, “for I will not deny you.”
units.rightText: Then she said, I ask one small petition of thee; deny me not. And the king said unto her, Ask on, my mother; for I will not deny thee.

units.leftText: So Bathsheba said, “Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as his wife.”
units.rightText: And she said, Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah thy brother to wife.

units.leftText: King Solomon answered his mother, “Why do you request Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Since he is my older brother, you might as well request the kingdom for him and for Abiathar the priest and for Joab son of Zeruiah!”
units.rightText: And king Solomon answered and said unto his mother, And why dost thou ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? ask for him the kingdom also; for he is mine elder brother; even for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab the son of Zeruiah.

units.leftText: Then King Solomon swore by the LORD: “May God punish me, and ever so severely, if Adonijah has not made this request at the expense of his life.
units.rightText: Then king Solomon sware by Jehovah, saying, God do so to me, and more also, if Adonijah hath not spoken this word against his own life.

units.leftText: And now, as surely as the LORD lives — the One who established me, who set me on the throne of my father David, and who founded for me a dynasty as He promised— surely Adonijah shall be put to death today!”
units.rightText: Now therefore as Jehovah liveth, who hath established me, and set me on the throne of David my father, and who hath made me a house, as he promised, surely Adonijah shall be put to death this day.

units.leftText: So King Solomon gave orders to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he struck down Adonijah and he died.
units.rightText: And king Solomon sent by Benaiah the son of Jehoiada; and he fell upon him, so that he died.

units.leftText: Then the king said to Abiathar the priest, “Go back to your fields in Anathoth. Even though you deserve to die, I will not put you to death at this time, since you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before my father David, and you suffered through all that my father suffered.”
units.rightText: And unto Abiathar the priest said the king, Get thee to Anathoth, unto thine own fields; for thou art worthy of death: but I will not at this time put thee to death, because thou barest the ark of the Lord Jehovah before David my father, and because thou wast afflicted in all wherein my father was afflicted.

units.leftText: So Solomon banished Abiathar from the priesthood of the LORD and thus fulfilled the word that the LORD had spoken at Shiloh against the house of Eli. The Execution of Joab
units.rightText: So Solomon thrust out Abiathar from being priest unto Jehovah, that he might fulfil the word of Jehovah, which he spake concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.

units.leftText: When the news reached Joab, who had conspired with Adonijah but not with Absalom, he fled to the tent of the LORD and took hold of the horns of the altar.
units.rightText: And the tidings came to Joab; for Joab had turned after Adonijah, though he turned not after Absalom. And Joab fled unto the Tent of Jehovah, and caught hold on the horns of the altar.

units.leftText: It was reported to King Solomon: “Joab has fled to the tent of the LORD and is now beside the altar.” So Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, “Go, strike him down!”
units.rightText: And it was told king Solomon, Joab is fled unto the Tent of Jehovah, and, behold, he is by the altar. Then Solomon sent Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, saying, Go, fall upon him.

units.leftText: And Benaiah entered the tent of the LORD and said to Joab, “The king says, ‘Come out!’” But Joab replied, “No, I will die here.” So Benaiah relayed the message to the king, saying, “This is how Joab answered me.”
units.rightText: And Benaiah came to the Tent of Jehovah, and said unto him, Thus saith the king, Come forth. And he said, Nay; but I will die here. And Benaiah brought the king word again, saying, Thus said Joab, and thus he answered me.

units.leftText: And the king replied, “Do just as he says. Strike him down and bury him, and so remove from me and from the house of my father the innocent blood that Joab shed.
units.rightText: And the king said unto him, Do as he hath said, and fall upon him, and bury him; that thou mayest take away the blood, which Joab shed without cause, from me and from my father’s house.

units.leftText: The LORD will bring his bloodshed back upon his own head, for without the knowledge of my father David he struck down two men more righteous and better than he when he put to the sword Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel’s army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah’s army.
units.rightText: And Jehovah will return his blood upon his own head, because he fell upon two men more righteous and better than he, and slew them with the sword, and my father David knew it not, to wit, Abner the son of Ner, captain of the host of Israel, and Amasa the son of Jether, captain of the host of Judah.

units.leftText: Their blood will come back upon the heads of Joab and his descendants forever; but for David, his descendants, his house, and his throne, there shall be peace from the LORD forever.”
units.rightText: So shall their blood return upon the head of Joab, and upon the head of his seed for ever: but unto David, and unto his seed, and unto his house, and unto his throne, shall there be peace for ever from Jehovah.

units.leftText: So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up, struck down Joab, and killed him. He was buried at his own home in the wilderness.
units.rightText: Then Benaiah the son of Jehoiada went up, and fell upon him, and slew him; and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.

units.leftText: And the king appointed Benaiah son of Jehoiada in Joab’s place over the army, and he appointed Zadok the priest in Abiathar’s place. The Execution of Shimei
units.rightText: And the king put Benaiah the son of Jehoiada in his room over the host; and Zadok the priest did the king put in the room of Abiathar.

units.leftText: Then the king summoned Shimei and said to him, “Build a house for yourself in Jerusalem and live there, but do not go anywhere else.
units.rightText: And the king sent and called for Shimei, and said unto him, Build thee a house in Jerusalem, and dwell there, and go not forth thence any whither.

units.leftText: On the day you go out and cross the Kidron Valley, know for sure that you will die; your blood will be on your own head.”
units.rightText: For on the day thou goest out, and passest over the brook Kidron, know thou for certain that thou shalt surely die: thy blood shall be upon thine own head.

units.leftText: “The sentence is fair,” Shimei replied. “Your servant will do as my lord the king has spoken.” And Shimei lived in Jerusalem for a long time.
units.rightText: And Shimei said unto the king, The saying is good: as my lord the king hath said, so will thy servant do. And Shimei dwelt in Jerusalem many days.

units.leftText: After three years, however, two of Shimei’s slaves ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. And Shimei was told, “Look, your slaves are in Gath.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass at the end of three years, that two of the servants of Shimei ran away unto Achish, son of Maacah, king of Gath. And they told Shimei, saying, Behold, thy servants are in Gath.
leftNotes: 2:39 Maacah is a variant of Maoch; see 1 Samuel 27:2|1SA 27:2*.

units.leftText: So Shimei saddled his donkey and set out to Achish at Gath in search of his slaves, and he brought them back from Gath.
units.rightText: And Shimei arose, and saddled his ass, and went to Gath to Achish, to seek his servants; and Shimei went, and brought his servants from Gath.

units.leftText: When Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had returned,
units.rightText: And it was told Solomon that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath, and was come again.

units.leftText: the king summoned Shimei and said to him, “Did I not make you swear by the LORD and warn you, ‘On the day you leave and go elsewhere, know for sure that you will die’? And you told me, ‘The sentence is fair; I will comply.’
units.rightText: And the king sent and called for Shimei, and said unto him, Did I not adjure thee by Jehovah, and protest unto thee, saying, Know for certain, that on the day thou goest out, and walkest abroad any whither, thou shalt surely die? and thou saidst unto me, The saying that I have heard is good.

units.leftText: So why have you not kept your oath to the LORD and the command that I gave you?”
units.rightText: Why then hast thou not kept the oath of Jehovah, and the commandment that I have charged thee with?

units.leftText: The king also said, “You know in your heart all the evil that you did to my father David. Therefore the LORD will bring your evil back upon your head.
units.rightText: The king said moreover to Shimei, Thou knowest all the wickedness which thy heart is privy to, that thou didst to David my father: therefore Jehovah shall return thy wickedness upon thine own head.

units.leftText: But King Solomon will be blessed and David’s throne will remain secure before the LORD forever.”
units.rightText: But king Solomon shall be blessed, and the throne of David shall be established before Jehovah for ever.

units.leftText: Then the king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and struck Shimei down, and he died. Thus the kingdom was firmly established in the hand of Solomon.
units.rightText: So the king commanded Benaiah the son of Jehoiada; and he went out, and fell upon him, so that he died. And the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon.

units.leftText: Later, Solomon formed an alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt by marrying his daughter. Solomon brought her to the City of David until he had finished building his palace and the house of the LORD, as well as the wall around Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And Solomon made affinity with Pharaoh king of Egypt, and took Pharaoh’s daughter, and brought her into the city of David, until he had made an end of building his own house, and the house of Jehovah, and the wall of Jerusalem round about.

units.leftText: The people, however, were still sacrificing on the high places because a house for the Name of the LORD had not yet been built.
units.rightText: Only the people sacrificed in the high places, because there was no house built for the name of Jehovah until those days.

units.leftText: And Solomon loved the LORD and walked in the statutes of his father David, except that he sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
units.rightText: And Solomon loved Jehovah, walking in the statutes of David his father: only he sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places.

units.leftText: Now the king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for it was the great high place. Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on the altar there.
units.rightText: And the king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there; for that was the great high place: a thousand burnt-offerings did Solomon offer upon that altar.

units.leftText: One night at Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream, and God said, “Ask, and I will give it to you!”
units.rightText: In Gibeon Jehovah appeared to Solomon in a dream by night; and God said, Ask what I shall give thee.

units.leftText: Solomon replied, “You have shown much loving devotion to Your servant, my father David, because he walked before You in faithfulness, righteousness, and uprightness of heart. And You have maintained this loving devotion by giving him a son to sit on his throne this very day.
units.rightText: And Solomon said, Thou hast showed unto thy servant David my father great lovingkindness, according as he walked before thee in truth, and in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with thee; and thou hast kept for him this great lovingkindness, that thou hast given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is this day.

units.leftText: And now, O LORD my God, You have made Your servant king in my father David’s place. But I am only a little child, not knowing how to go out or come in.
units.rightText: And now, O Jehovah my God, thou hast made thy servant king instead of David my father: and I am but a little child; I know not how to go out or come in.

units.leftText: Your servant is here among the people You have chosen, a people too numerous to count or number.
units.rightText: And thy servant is in the midst of thy people which thou hast chosen, a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude.

units.leftText: Therefore give Your servant an understanding heart to judge Your people and to discern between good and evil. For who is able to govern this great people of Yours?”
units.rightText: Give thy servant therefore an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and evil; for who is able to judge this thy great people?

units.leftText: Now it pleased the Lord that Solomon had made this request.
units.rightText: And the speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.
leftNotes: 3:10 Hebrew Adonai; also in verse 15

units.leftText: So God said to him, “Since you have asked for this instead of requesting long life or wealth for yourself or death for your enemies — but you have asked for discernment to administer justice —
units.rightText: And God said unto him, Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life, neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies, but hast asked for thyself understanding to discern justice;

units.leftText: behold, I will do what you have asked. I will give you a wise and discerning heart, so that there will never have been another like you, nor will there ever be.
units.rightText: behold, I have done according to thy word: lo, I have given thee a wise and an understanding heart; so that there hath been none like thee before thee, neither after thee shall any arise like unto thee.

units.leftText: Moreover, I will give you what you did not request — both riches and honor — so that during all your days no man in any kingdom will be your equal.
units.rightText: And I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches and honor, so that there shall not be any among the kings like unto thee, all thy days.

units.leftText: So if you walk in My ways and keep My statutes and commandments, just as your father David did, I will prolong your days.”
units.rightText: And if thou wilt walk in my ways, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as thy father David did walk, then I will lengthen thy days.

units.leftText: Then Solomon awoke, and indeed it had been a dream. So he returned to Jerusalem, stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then he held a feast for all his servants. Solomon Judges Wisely
units.rightText: And Solomon awoke; and, behold, it was a dream: and he came to Jerusalem, and stood before the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, and offered up burnt-offerings, and offered peace-offerings, and made a feast to all his servants.

units.leftText: At that time two prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.
units.rightText: Then there came two women that were harlots, unto the king, and stood before him.

units.leftText: One woman said, “Please, my lord, this woman and I live in the same house, and I gave birth while she was in the house.
units.rightText: And the one woman said, Oh, my lord, I and this woman dwell in one house; and I was delivered of a child with her in the house.

units.leftText: On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also had a baby. We were alone, with no one in the house but the two of us.
units.rightText: And it came to pass the third day after I was delivered, that this woman was delivered also; and we were together; there was no stranger with us in the house, save we two in the house.

units.leftText: During the night this woman’s son died because she rolled over on him.
units.rightText: And this woman’s child died in the night, because she lay upon it.

units.leftText: So she got up in the middle of the night and took my son from my side while I was asleep. She laid him in her bosom and put her dead son at my bosom.
units.rightText: And she arose at midnight, and took my son from beside me, while thy handmaid slept, and laid it in her bosom, and laid her dead child in my bosom.

units.leftText: The next morning, when I got up to nurse my son, I discovered he was dead. But when I examined him, I realized that he was not the son I had borne.”
units.rightText: And when I rose in the morning to give my child suck, behold, it was dead; but when I had looked at it in the morning, behold, it was not my son, whom I did bear.

units.leftText: “No,” said the other woman, “the living one is my son and the dead one is your son.” But the first woman insisted, “No, the dead one is yours and the living one is mine.” So they argued before the king.
units.rightText: And the other woman said, Nay; but the living is my son, and the dead is thy son. And this said, No; but the dead is thy son, and the living is my son. Thus they spake before the king.

units.leftText: Then the king replied, “This woman says, ‘My son is alive and yours is dead,’ but that woman says, ‘No, your son is dead and mine is alive.’”
units.rightText: Then said the king, The one saith, This is my son that liveth, and thy son is the dead: and the other saith, Nay; but thy son is the dead, and my son is the living.

units.leftText: The king continued, “Bring me a sword.” So they brought him a sword,
units.rightText: And the king said, Fetch me a sword. And they brought a sword before the king.

units.leftText: and the king declared, “Cut the living child in two and give half to one and half to the other.”
units.rightText: And the king said, Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other.

units.leftText: Then the woman whose son was alive spoke to the king because she yearned with compassion for her son. “Please, my lord,” she said, “give her the living baby. Do not kill him!” But the other woman said, “He will be neither mine nor yours. Cut him in two!”
units.rightText: Then spake the woman whose the living child was unto the king, for her heart yearned over her son, and she said, Oh, my lord, give her the living child, and in no wise slay it. But the other said, It shall be neither mine nor thine; divide it.

units.leftText: Then the king gave his ruling: “Give the living baby to the first woman. By no means should you kill him; she is his mother.”
units.rightText: Then the king answered and said, Give her the living child, and in no wise slay it: she is the mother thereof.

units.leftText: When all Israel heard of the judgment the king had given, they stood in awe of him, for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to administer justice.
units.rightText: And all Israel heard of the judgment which the king had judged; and they feared the king: for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him, to do justice.

units.leftText: So King Solomon ruled over Israel,
units.rightText: And king Solomon was king over all Israel.

units.leftText: and these were his chief officials: Azariah son of Zadok was the priest;
units.rightText: And these were the princes whom he had: Azariah the son of Zadok, the priest;

units.leftText: Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, were secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;
units.rightText: Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, scribes; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud, the recorder;
leftNotes: 4:3 Shisha is also called Seraiah, Sheva, and Shavsha; see 2 Samuel 8:17|2SA 8:17*, 2 Samuel 20:25, and 1 Chronicles 18:16.

units.leftText: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was in charge of the army; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
units.rightText: and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the host; and Zadok and Abiathar were priests;

units.leftText: Azariah son of Nathan was in charge of the governors; Zabud son of Nathan was a priest and adviser to the king;
units.rightText: and Azariah the son of Nathan was over the officers; and Zabud the son of Nathan was chief minister, and the king’s friend;

units.leftText: Ahishar was in charge of the palace; and Adoniram son of Abda was in charge of the forced labor. Solomon’s Twelve Officers
units.rightText: and Ahishar was over the household; and Adoniram the son of Abda was over the men subject to taskwork.
leftNotes: 4:6 Adoniram is a variant of Adoram and Hadoram; see 2 Samuel 20:24|2SA 20:24* and 2 Chronicles 10:18.

units.leftText: Solomon had twelve governors over all Israel to provide food for the king and his household. Each one would arrange provisions for one month of the year,
units.rightText: And Solomon had twelve officers over all Israel, who provided victuals for the king and his household: each man had to make provision for a month in the year.

units.leftText: and these were their names: Ben-hur in the hill country of Ephraim;
units.rightText: And these are their names: Ben-hur, in the hill-country of Ephraim;

units.leftText: Ben-deker in Makaz, in Shaalbim, in Beth-shemesh, and in Elon-beth-hanan;
units.rightText: Ben-deker, in Makaz, and in Shaalbim, and Beth-shemesh, and Elon-beth-hanan;

units.leftText: Ben-hesed in Arubboth (Socoh and all the land of Hepher belonged to him);
units.rightText: Ben-hesed, in Arubboth (to him pertained Socoh, and all the land of Hepher);

units.leftText: Ben-abinadab in Naphath-dor (Taphath, a daughter of Solomon, was his wife);
units.rightText: Ben-abinadab, in all the height of Dor (he had Taphath the daughter of Solomon to wife);
leftNotes: 4:11 Or in all the heights of Dor; Naphath-dor is a variant of Naphoth-dor; see Joshua 11:2|JOS 11:2*.

units.leftText: Baana son of Ahilud in Taanach, in Megiddo, and in all of Beth-shean next to Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah and on past Jokmeam;
units.rightText: Baana the son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Megiddo, and all Beth-shean which is beside Zarethan, beneath Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as beyond Jokmeam;

units.leftText: Ben-geber in Ramoth-gilead (the villages of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead belonged to him, as well as the region of Argob in Bashan with its sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars);
units.rightText: Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead (to him pertained the towns of Jair the son of Manasseh, which are in Gilead; even to him pertained the region of Argob, which is in Bashan, threescore great cities with walls and brazen bars);

units.leftText: Ahinadab son of Iddo in Mahanaim;
units.rightText: Ahinadab the son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;

units.leftText: Ahimaaz in Naphtali (he had married Basemath, a daughter of Solomon) ;
units.rightText: Ahimaaz, in Naphtali (he also took Basemath the daughter of Solomon to wife);

units.leftText: Baana son of Hushai in Asher and in Aloth;
units.rightText: Baana the son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;

units.leftText: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah in Issachar;
units.rightText: Jehoshaphat the son of Paruah, in Issachar;

units.leftText: Shimei son of Ela in Benjamin;
units.rightText: Shimei the son of Ela, in Benjamin;

units.leftText: Geber son of Uri in the land of Gilead, including the territories of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan. There was also one governor in the land of Judah. Solomon’s Prosperity
units.rightText: Geber the son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the country of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan; and he was the only officer that was in the land.
leftNotes: 4:19 Some LXX manuscripts; Hebrew And he was the one governor in the land.

units.leftText: The people of Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand on the seashore, and they were eating and drinking and rejoicing.
units.rightText: Judah and Israel were many as the sand which is by the sea in multitude, eating and drinking and making merry.

units.leftText: And Solomon reigned over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt. These kingdoms offered tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.
units.rightText: And Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the River unto the land of the Philistines, and unto the border of Egypt: they brought tribute, and served Solomon all the days of his life.
leftNotes: 4:21 Hebrew the River; also in verse 24

units.leftText: Solomon’s provisions for a single day were thirty cors of fine flour, sixty cors of meal,
units.rightText: And Solomon’s provision for one day was thirty measures of fine flour, and threescore measures of meal,
leftNotes: 4:22 30 cors is approximately 187 bushels or 6,600 liters (probably about 5.5 tons or 5 metric tons of flour).
4:22 60 cors is approximately 375 bushels or 13,200 liters (probably about 11 tons or 10 metric tons of meal).

units.leftText: ten fat oxen, twenty range oxen, and a hundred sheep, as well as deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened poultry.
units.rightText: ten fat oxen, and twenty oxen out of the pastures, and a hundred sheep, besides harts, and gazelles, and roebucks, and fatted fowl.

units.leftText: For Solomon had dominion over everything west of the Euphrates — over all the kingdoms from Tiphsah to Gaza — and he had peace on all sides.
units.rightText: For he had dominion over all the region on this side the River, from Tiphsah even to Gaza, over all the kings on this side the River: and he had peace on all sides round about him.
leftNotes: 4:24 Or beyond the River

units.leftText: Throughout the days of Solomon, Judah and Israel dwelt securely from Dan to Beersheba, each man under his own vine and his own fig tree.
units.rightText: And Judah and Israel dwelt safely, every man under his vine and under his fig-tree, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, all the days of Solomon.

units.leftText: Solomon had 4,000 stalls for his chariot horses and 12,000 horses.
units.rightText: And Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen.
leftNotes: 4:26 Some LXX manuscripts (see also 2 Chronicles 9:25|2CH 9:25*); Hebrew 40,000
4:26 Or horsemen or charioteers

units.leftText: Each month the governors in turn provided food for King Solomon and all who came to his table. They saw to it that nothing was lacking.
units.rightText: And those officers provided victuals for king Solomon, and for all that came unto king Solomon’s table, every man in his month; they let nothing be lacking.

units.leftText: Each one also brought to the required place their quotas of barley and straw for the chariot horses and other horses. Solomon’s Wisdom
units.rightText: Barley also and straw for the horses and swift steeds brought they unto the place where the officers were, every man according to his charge.

units.leftText: And God gave Solomon wisdom, exceedingly deep insight, and understanding beyond measure, like the sand on the seashore.
units.rightText: And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart, even as the sand that is on the sea-shore.

units.leftText: Solomon’s wisdom was greater than that of all the men of the East, greater than all the wisdom of Egypt.
units.rightText: And Solomon’s wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east, and all the wisdom of Egypt.

units.leftText: He was wiser than all men— wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and wiser than Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol. And his fame spread throughout the surrounding nations.
units.rightText: For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all the nations round about.

units.leftText: Solomon composed three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered a thousand and five.
units.rightText: And he spake three thousand proverbs; and his songs were a thousand and five.

units.leftText: He spoke of trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing in the wall, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.
units.rightText: And he spake of trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon even unto the hyssop that springeth out of the wall; he spake also of beasts, and of birds, and of creeping things, and of fishes.

units.leftText: So men of all nations came to listen to Solomon’s wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom.
units.rightText: And there came of all peoples to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom.

units.leftText: Now when Hiram king of Tyre heard that Solomon had been anointed king in his father’s place, he sent envoys to Solomon; for Hiram had always been a friend of David.
units.rightText: And Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants unto Solomon; for he had heard that they had anointed him king in the room of his father: for Hiram was ever a lover of David.

units.leftText: And Solomon relayed this message to Hiram:
units.rightText: And Solomon sent to Hiram, saying,

units.leftText: “As you are well aware, due to the wars waged on all sides against my father David, he could not build a house for the Name of the LORD his God until the LORD had put his enemies under his feet.
units.rightText: Thou knowest how that David my father could not build a house for the name of Jehovah his God for the wars which were about him on every side, until Jehovah put them under the soles of his feet.

units.leftText: But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side, and there is no adversary or crisis.
units.rightText: But now Jehovah my God hath given me rest on every side; there is neither adversary, nor evil occurrence.

units.leftText: So behold, I plan to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God, according to what the LORD said to my father David: ‘I will put your son on your throne in your place, and he will build the house for My Name.’
units.rightText: And, behold, I purpose to build a house for the name of Jehovah my God, as Jehovah spake unto David my father, saying, Thy son, whom I will set upon thy throne in thy room, he shall build the house for my name.

units.leftText: Now therefore, order that cedars of Lebanon be cut down for me. My servants will be with your servants, and I will pay your servants whatever wages you set, for you know that there are none among us as skilled in logging as the Sidonians.” Hiram’s Reply to Solomon (2 Chronicles 2:11–18|2CH 2:11-18*)
units.rightText: Now therefore command thou that they cut me cedar-trees out of Lebanon; and my servants shall be with thy servants; and I will give thee hire for thy servants according to all that thou shalt say: for thou knowest that there is not among us any that knoweth how to cut timber like unto the Sidonians.

units.leftText: When Hiram received Solomon’s message, he rejoiced greatly and said, “Blessed be the LORD this day! He has given David a wise son over this great people!”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Hiram heard the words of Solomon, that he rejoiced greatly, and said, Blessed be Jehovah this day, who hath given unto David a wise son over this great people.

units.leftText: Then Hiram sent a reply to Solomon, saying:
units.rightText: And Hiram sent to Solomon, saying, I have heard the message which thou hast sent unto me: I will do all thy desire concerning timber of cedar, and concerning timber of fir.

units.leftText: My servants will haul the logs from Lebanon to the Sea, and I will float them as rafts by sea to the place you specify. There I will separate the logs, and you can take them away. And in exchange, you can meet my needs by providing my household with food.”
units.rightText: My servants shall bring them down from Lebanon unto the sea; and I will make them into rafts to go by sea unto the place that thou shalt appoint me, and will cause them to be broken up there, and thou shalt receive them; and thou shalt accomplish my desire, in giving food for my household.
leftNotes: 5:9 That is, the Mediterranean Sea, also called the Great Sea

units.leftText: So Hiram provided Solomon with all the cedar and cypress timber he wanted,
units.rightText: So Hiram gave Solomon timber of cedar and timber of fir according to all his desire.

units.leftText: and year after year Solomon would provide Hiram with 20,000 cors of wheat as food for his household, as well as 20,000 baths of pure olive oil.
units.rightText: And Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand measures of wheat for food to his household, and twenty measures of pure oil: thus gave Solomon to Hiram year by year.
leftNotes: 5:11 20,000 cors is approximately 124,800 bushels or 4.4 million liters (probably about 3,800 tons or 3,400 metric tons of wheat).
5:11 LXX (see also 2 Chronicles 2:10|2CH 2:10*); 20,000 baths is approximately 116,000 gallons or 440,000 liters of olive oil; Hebrew twenty cors of pure oil or twenty cors of pressed oil

units.leftText: And the LORD gave Solomon wisdom, as He had promised him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a treaty. Solomon’s Labor Force
units.rightText: And Jehovah gave Solomon wisdom, as he promised him; and there was peace between Hiram and Solomon; and they two made a league together.
leftNotes: 5:12 Forms of the Hebrew berit are translated in most passages as covenant.

units.leftText: Then King Solomon conscripted a labor force of 30,000 men from all Israel.
units.rightText: And king Solomon raised a levy out of all Israel; and the levy was thirty thousand men.

units.leftText: He sent them to Lebanon in monthly shifts of 10,000 men, so that they would spend one month in Lebanon and two months at home. And Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor.
units.rightText: And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month by courses; a month they were in Lebanon, and two months at home: and Adoniram was over the men subject to taskwork.

units.leftText: Solomon had 70,000 porters and 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains,
units.rightText: And Solomon had threescore and ten thousand that bare burdens, and fourscore thousand that were hewers in the mountains;

units.leftText: not including his 3,300 foremen who supervised the workers.
units.rightText: besides Solomon’s chief officers that were over the work, three thousand and three hundred, who bare rule over the people that wrought in the work.
leftNotes: 5:16 Hebrew; some LXX manuscripts 3,600; see 2 Chronicles 2:18|2CH 2:18*.

units.leftText: And the king commanded them to quarry large, costly stones to lay the foundation of the temple with dressed stones.
units.rightText: And the king commanded, and they hewed out great stones, costly stones, to lay the foundation of the house with wrought stone.

units.leftText: So Solomon’s and Hiram’s builders, along with the Gebalites, quarried the stone and prepared the timber and stone for the construction of the temple.
units.rightText: And Solomon’s builders and Hiram’s builders and the Gebalites did fashion them, and prepared the timber and the stones to build the house.

units.leftText: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, the second month, he began to build the house of the LORD.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel were come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month Ziv, which is the second month, that he began to build the house of Jehovah.
leftNotes: 6:1 Hebrew; LXX four hundred and fortieth
6:1 Ziv was the second month of the ancient Hebrew lunar calendar, usually occurring within the months of April and May; also in verse 37.

units.leftText: The house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
units.rightText: And the house which king Solomon built for Jehovah, the length thereof was threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof twenty cubits, and the height thereof thirty cubits.
leftNotes: 6:2 The house was approximately 90 feet long, 30 feet wide, and 45 feet high (27.4 meters long, 9.1 meters wide, and 13.7 meters high).

units.leftText: The portico at the front of the main hall of the temple was twenty cubits long, extending across the width of the temple and projecting out ten cubits in front of the temple.
units.rightText: And the porch before the temple of the house, twenty cubits was the length thereof, according to the breadth of the house; and ten cubits was the breadth thereof before the house.
leftNotes: 6:3 20 cubits is approximately 30 feet or 9.1 meters; also in verses 16 and 20.
6:3 10 cubits is approximately 15 feet or 4.6 meters; also in verses 23–26.

units.leftText: He also had narrow windows framed high in the temple. The Chambers
units.rightText: And for the house he made windows of fixed lattice-work.

units.leftText: Against the walls of the temple and the inner sanctuary, Solomon built a chambered structure around the temple, in which he constructed the side rooms.
units.rightText: And against the wall of the house he built stories round about, against the walls of the house round about, both of the temple and of the oracle; and he made side-chambers round about.

units.leftText: The bottom floor was five cubits wide, the middle floor six cubits, and the third floor seven cubits. He also placed offset ledges around the outside of the temple, so that nothing would be inserted into its walls.
units.rightText: The nethermost story was five cubits broad, and the middle was six cubits broad, and the third was seven cubits broad; for on the outside he made offsets in the wall of the house round about, that the beams should not have hold in the walls of the house.
leftNotes: 6:6 5 cubits is approximately 7.5 feet or 2.3 meters; also in verses 10 and 24.
6:6 6 cubits is approximately 9 feet or 2.7 meters.
6:6 7 cubits is approximately 10.5 feet or 3.2 meters.

units.leftText: The temple was constructed using finished stones cut at the quarry, so that no hammer or chisel or any other iron tool was heard in the temple while it was being built.
units.rightText: And the house, when it was in building, was built of stone made ready at the quarry; and there was neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron heard in the house, while it was in building.

units.leftText: The entrance to the bottom floor was on the south side of the temple. A stairway led up to the middle level, and from there to the third floor.
units.rightText: The door for the middle side-chambers was in the right side of the house: and they went up by winding stairs into the middle story, and out of the middle into the third.
leftNotes: 6:8 LXX and Targum; Hebrew middle

units.leftText: So Solomon built the temple and finished it, roofing it with beams and planks of cedar.
units.rightText: So he built the house, and finished it; and he covered the house with beams and planks of cedar.

units.leftText: He built chambers all along the temple, each five cubits high and attached to the temple with beams of cedar. God’s Promise to Solomon
units.rightText: And he built the stories against all the house, each five cubits high: and they rested on the house with timber of cedar.

units.leftText: Then the word of the LORD came to Solomon, saying:
units.rightText: And the word of Jehovah came to Solomon, saying,

units.leftText: “As for this temple you are building, if you walk in My statutes, carry out My ordinances, and keep all My commandments by walking in them, I will fulfill through you the promise I made to your father David.
units.rightText: Concerning this house which thou art building, if thou wilt walk in my statutes, and execute mine ordinances, and keep all my commandments to walk in them; then will I establish my word with thee, which I spake unto David thy father.

units.leftText: And I will dwell among the Israelites and will not abandon My people Israel.” The Temple’s Interior (2 Chronicles 3:5–9|2CH 3:5-9*)
units.rightText: And I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will not forsake my people Israel.

units.leftText: So Solomon built the temple and finished it.
units.rightText: So Solomon built the house, and finished it.

units.leftText: He lined the interior walls with cedar paneling from the floor of the temple to the ceiling, and he covered the floor with cypress boards.
units.rightText: And he built the walls of the house within with boards of cedar: from the floor of the house unto the walls of the ceiling, he covered them on the inside with wood; and he covered the floor of the house with boards of fir.
leftNotes: 6:15 Or pine or juniper or fir; also in verse 34

units.leftText: He partitioned off the twenty cubits at the rear of the temple with cedar boards from floor to ceiling to form within the temple an inner sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.
units.rightText: And he built twenty cubits on the hinder part of the house with boards of cedar from the floor unto the walls of the ceiling: he built them for it within, for an oracle, even for the most holy place.
leftNotes: 6:16 Or the Holy of Holies

units.leftText: And the main hall in front of this room was forty cubits long.
units.rightText: And the house, that is, the temple before the oracle, was forty cubits long.
leftNotes: 6:17 40 cubits is approximately 60 feet or 18.3 meters.

units.leftText: The cedar paneling inside the temple was carved with gourds and open flowers. Everything was cedar; not a stone could be seen.
units.rightText: And there was cedar on the house within, carved with knops and open flowers: all was cedar; there was no stone seen.

units.leftText: Solomon also prepared the inner sanctuary within the temple to set the ark of the covenant of the LORD there.
units.rightText: And he prepared an oracle in the midst of the house within, to set there the ark of the covenant of Jehovah.

units.leftText: The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He overlaid the inside with pure gold, and he also overlaid the altar of cedar.
units.rightText: And within the oracle was a space of twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in breadth, and twenty cubits in the height thereof; and he overlaid it with pure gold: and he covered the altar with cedar.
leftNotes: 6:20 Or with cedar

units.leftText: So Solomon overlaid the inside of the temple with pure gold, and he extended gold chains across the front of the inner sanctuary, which was overlaid with gold.
units.rightText: So Solomon overlaid the house within with pure gold: and he drew chains of gold across before the oracle; and he overlaid it with gold.
leftNotes: 6:21 Or made gold chains to draw (the curtains)

units.leftText: So he overlaid with gold the whole interior of the temple, until everything was completely finished. He also overlaid with gold the entire altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary. The Cherubim (2 Chronicles 3:10–13|2CH 3:10-13*)
units.rightText: And the whole house he overlaid with gold, until all the house was finished: also the whole altar that belonged to the oracle he overlaid with gold.

units.leftText: In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim, each ten cubits high, out of olive wood.
units.rightText: And in the oracle he made two cherubim of olive-wood, each ten cubits high.

units.leftText: One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long, and the other wing was five cubits long as well. So the full wingspan was ten cubits.
units.rightText: And five cubits was the one wing of the cherub, and five cubits the other wing of the cherub: from the uttermost part of the one wing unto the uttermost part of the other were ten cubits.

units.leftText: The second cherub also measured ten cubits; both cherubim had the same size and shape,
units.rightText: And the other cherub was ten cubits: both the cherubim were of one measure and one form.

units.leftText: and the height of each cherub was ten cubits.
units.rightText: The height of the one cherub was ten cubits, and so was it of the other cherub.

units.leftText: And he placed the cherubim inside the innermost room of the temple. Since their wings were spread out, the wing of the first cherub touched one wall, while the wing of the second cherub touched the other wall, and in the middle of the room their wingtips touched.
units.rightText: And he set the cherubim within the inner house; and the wings of the cherubim were stretched forth, so that the wing of the one touched the one wall, and the wing of the other cherub touched the other wall; and their wings touched one another in the midst of the house.

units.leftText: He also overlaid the cherubim with gold.
units.rightText: And he overlaid the cherubim with gold.

units.leftText: Then he carved the walls all around the temple, in both the inner and outer sanctuaries, with carved engravings of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers.
units.rightText: And he carved all the walls of the house round about with carved figures of cherubim and palm-trees and open flowers, within and without.

units.leftText: And he overlaid the temple floor with gold in both the inner and outer sanctuaries. The Doors
units.rightText: And the floor of the house he overlaid with gold, within and without.

units.leftText: For the entrance to the inner sanctuary, Solomon constructed doors of olive wood with five-sided doorposts.
units.rightText: And for the entrance of the oracle he made doors of olive-wood: the lintel and door-posts were a fifth part of the wall.

units.leftText: The double doors were made of olive wood, and he carved into them cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers and overlaid the cherubim and palm trees with hammered gold.
units.rightText: So he made two doors of olive-wood; and he carved upon them carvings of cherubim and palm-trees and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold; and he spread the gold upon the cherubim, and upon the palm-trees.

units.leftText: In the same way he made four-sided doorposts of olive wood for the sanctuary entrance.
units.rightText: So also made he for the entrance of the temple door-posts of olive-wood, out of a fourth part of the wall;

units.leftText: The two doors were made of cypress wood, and each had two folding panels.
units.rightText: and two doors of fir-wood: the two leaves of the one door were folding, and the two leaves of the other door were folding.

units.leftText: He carved into them cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and he overlaid them with gold hammered evenly over the carvings. The Courtyard
units.rightText: And he carved thereon cherubim and palm-trees and open flowers; and he overlaid them with gold fitted upon the graven work.

units.leftText: Solomon built the inner courtyard with three rows of dressed stone and one row of trimmed cedar beams.
units.rightText: And he built the inner court with three courses of hewn stone, and a course of cedar beams.

units.leftText: The foundation of the house of the LORD was laid in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign, in the month of Ziv.
units.rightText: In the fourth year was the foundation of the house of Jehovah laid, in the month Ziv.

units.leftText: In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, the eighth month, the temple was finished in every detail and according to every specification. So he built the temple in seven years.
units.rightText: And in the eleventh year, in the month Bul, which is the eighth month, was the house finished throughout all the parts thereof, and according to all the fashion of it. So was he seven years in building it.
leftNotes: 6:38 Bul was the eighth month of the ancient Hebrew lunar calendar, usually occurring within the months of October and November.

units.leftText: Solomon, however, took thirteen years to complete the construction of his entire palace.
units.rightText: And Solomon was building his own house thirteen years, and he finished all his house.

units.leftText: He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high, with four rows of cedar pillars supporting the cedar beams.
units.rightText: For he built the house of the forest of Lebanon; the length thereof was a hundred cubits, and the breadth thereof fifty cubits, and the height thereof thirty cubits, upon four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams upon the pillars.
leftNotes: 7:2 The house was approximately 150 feet long, 75 feet wide, and 45 feet high (45.7 meters long, 22.9 meters wide, and 13.7 meters high).

units.leftText: The house was roofed with cedar above the beams that rested on the pillars — forty-five beams, fifteen per row.
units.rightText: And it was covered with cedar above over the forty and five beams, that were upon the pillars; fifteen in a row.

units.leftText: There were three rows of high windows facing one another in three tiers.
units.rightText: And there were beams in three rows, and window was over against window in three ranks.

units.leftText: All the doorways had rectangular frames, with the openings facing one another in three tiers.
units.rightText: And all the doors and posts were made square with beams: and window was over against window in three ranks.
leftNotes: 7:5 Literally doorways and doorposts

units.leftText: Solomon made his colonnade fifty cubits long and thirty cubits wide, with a portico in front of it and a canopy with pillars in front of the portico.
units.rightText: And he made the porch of pillars; the length thereof was fifty cubits, and the breadth thereof thirty cubits; and a porch before them; and pillars and a threshold before them.
leftNotes: 7:6 The colonnade was approximately 75 feet long and 45 feet wide (22.9 meters long and 13.7 meters wide).

units.leftText: In addition, he built a hall for the throne, the Hall of Justice, where he was to judge. It was paneled with cedar from floor to ceiling.
units.rightText: And he made the porch of the throne where he was to judge, even the porch of judgment: and it was covered with cedar from floor to floor.
leftNotes: 7:7 Syriac and Vulgate; Hebrew from floor to floor

units.leftText: And the palace where Solomon would live, set further back, was of similar construction. He also made a palace like this hall for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom he had married.
units.rightText: And his house where he was to dwell, the other court within the porch, was of the like work. He made also a house for Pharaoh’s daughter (whom Solomon had taken to wife), like unto this porch.

units.leftText: All these buildings were constructed with costly stones, cut to size and trimmed with saws inside and out from the foundation to the eaves, and from the outside to the great courtyard.
units.rightText: All these were of costly stones, even of hewn stone, according to measure, sawed with saws, within and without, even from the foundation unto the coping, and so on the outside unto the great court.

units.leftText: The foundations were laid with large, costly stones, some ten cubits long and some eight cubits long.
units.rightText: And the foundation was of costly stones, even great stones, stones of ten cubits, and stones of eight cubits.
leftNotes: 7:10 10 cubits is approximately 15 feet or 4.6 meters.
7:10 8 cubits is approximately 12 feet or 3.7 meters.

units.leftText: Above these were costly stones, cut to size, and cedar beams.
units.rightText: And above were costly stones, even hewn stone, according to measure, and cedar-wood.

units.leftText: The great courtyard was surrounded by three rows of dressed stone and a row of trimmed cedar beams, as were the inner courtyard and portico of the house of the LORD. The Pillars and Capitals (2 Chronicles 3:14–17|2CH 3:14-17*)
units.rightText: And the great court round about had three courses of hewn stone, and a course of cedar beams; like as the inner court of the house of Jehovah, and the porch of the house.

units.leftText: Now King Solomon sent to bring Huram from Tyre.
units.rightText: And king Solomon sent and fetched Hiram out of Tyre.
leftNotes: 7:13 Hebrew Hiram, a variant of Huram; also in verses 40 and 45; see 2 Chronicles 4:11|2CH 4:11*. Note that this is not Hiram king of Tyre mentioned in 1 Kings 5:1.

units.leftText: He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a craftsman in bronze. Huram had great skill, understanding, and knowledge for every kind of bronze work. So he came to King Solomon and carried out all his work.
units.rightText: He was the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in brass; and he was filled with wisdom and understanding and skill, to work all works in brass. And he came to king Solomon, and wrought all his work.

units.leftText: He cast two pillars of bronze, each eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits in circumference.
units.rightText: For he fashioned the two pillars of brass, eighteen cubits high apiece: and a line of twelve cubits compassed either of them about.
leftNotes: 7:15 Each pillar was approximately 27 feet high and 18 feet in circumference (8.2 meters high and 5.5 meters in circumference).

units.leftText: He also made two capitals of cast bronze to set on top of the pillars, each capital five cubits high.
units.rightText: And he made two capitals of molten brass, to set upon the tops of the pillars: the height of the one capital was five cubits, and the height of the other capital was five cubits.
leftNotes: 7:16 5 cubits is approximately 7.5 feet or 2.3 meters.

units.leftText: For the capitals on top of the pillars he made a network of lattice, with wreaths of chainwork, seven for each capital.
units.rightText: There were nets of checker-work, and wreaths of chain-work, for the capitals which were upon the top of the pillars; seven for the one capital, and seven for the other capital.
leftNotes: 7:17 Hebrew; LXX one for each capital

units.leftText: Likewise, he made the pillars with two rows of pomegranates around each grating to cover each capital atop the pillars.
units.rightText: So he made the pillars; and there were two rows round about upon the one network, to cover the capitals that were upon the top of the pillars: and so did he for the other capital.

units.leftText: And the capitals atop the pillars in the portico were shaped like lilies, four cubits high.
units.rightText: And the capitals that were upon the top of the pillars in the porch were of lily-work, four cubits.
leftNotes: 7:19 4 cubits is approximately 6 feet or 1.8 meters; also in verse 38.

units.leftText: On the capitals of both pillars, just above the rounded projection next to the network, were the two hundred pomegranates in rows encircling each capital.
units.rightText: And there were capitals above also upon the two pillars, close by the belly which was beside the network: and the pomegranates were two hundred, in rows round about upon the other capital.

units.leftText: Thus he set up the pillars at the portico of the temple. The pillar to the south he named Jachin, and the pillar to the north he named Boaz.
units.rightText: And he set up the pillars at the porch of the temple: and he set up the right pillar, and called the name thereof Jachin; and he set up the left pillar, and called the name thereof Boaz.
leftNotes: 7:21 Jachin probably means He establishes.
7:21 Boaz probably means in Him is strength.
