units.leftText: And the tops of the pillars were shaped like lilies. So the work of the pillars was completed. The Molten Sea (2 Chronicles 4:1–5|2CH 4:1-5*)
units.rightText: And upon the top of the pillars was lily-work: so was the work of the pillars finished.

units.leftText: He also made the Sea of cast metal. It was circular in shape, measuring ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits in height, and thirty cubits in circumference.
units.rightText: And he made the molten sea of ten cubits from brim to brim, round in compass, and the height thereof was five cubits; and a line of thirty cubits compassed it round about.
leftNotes: 7:23 The Sea was approximately 15 feet from rim to rim, 7.5 feet in height, and 45 feet in circumference (4.6 meters from rim to rim, 2.3 meters in height, and 13.7 meters in circumference).

units.leftText: Below the rim, ornamental buds encircled it, ten per cubit all the way around the Sea, cast in two rows as a part of the Sea.
units.rightText: And under the brim of it round about there were knops which did compass it, for ten cubits, compassing the sea round about: the knops were in two rows, cast when it was cast.

units.leftText: The Sea stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The Sea rested on them, with all their hindquarters toward the center.
units.rightText: It stood upon twelve oxen, three looking toward the north, and three looking toward the west, and three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east; and the sea was set upon them above, and all their hinder parts were inward.

units.leftText: It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was fashioned like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It could hold two thousand baths. The Ten Bronze Stands
units.rightText: And it was a handbreadth thick: and the brim thereof was wrought like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily: it held two thousand baths.
leftNotes: 7:26 A handbreadth is approximately 2.9 inches or 7.4 centimeters.
7:26 2,000 baths is approximately 11,600 gallons or 44,000 liters; LXX does not include this sentence.

units.leftText: In addition, he made ten movable stands of bronze, each four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits high.
units.rightText: And he made the ten bases of brass; four cubits was the length of one base, and four cubits the breadth thereof, and three cubits the height of it.
leftNotes: 7:27 The stands were approximately 6 feet in length and width, and 4.5 feet high (1.8 meters in length and width, and 1.4 meters high).

units.leftText: This was the design of the stands: They had side panels attached to uprights,
units.rightText: And the work of the bases was on this manner: they had panels; and there were panels between the ledges;

units.leftText: and on the panels between the uprights were lions, oxen, and cherubim. On the uprights was a pedestal above, and below the lions and oxen were wreaths of beveled work.
units.rightText: and on the panels that were between the ledges were lions, oxen, and cherubim; and upon the ledges there was a pedestal above; and beneath the lions and oxen were wreaths of hanging work.

units.leftText: Each stand had four bronze wheels with bronze axles and a basin resting on four supports, with wreaths at each side.
units.rightText: And every base had four brazen wheels, and axles of brass; and the four feet thereof had undersetters: beneath the laver were the undersetters molten, with wreaths at the side of each.

units.leftText: The opening to each stand inside the crown at the top was one cubit deep, with a round opening like the design of a pedestal, a cubit and a half wide. And around its opening were engravings, but the panels of the stands were square, not round.
units.rightText: And the mouth of it within the capital and above was a cubit: and the mouth thereof was round after the work of a pedestal, a cubit and a half; and also upon the mouth of it were gravings, and their panels were foursquare, not round.
leftNotes: 7:31 One cubit is approximately 18 inches or 45.7 centimeters.
7:31 A cubit and a half is approximately 2.25 feet or 68.6 centimeters wide; similarly in verse 32.

units.leftText: There were four wheels under the panels, and the axles of the wheels were attached to the stand; each wheel was a cubit and a half in diameter.
units.rightText: And the four wheels were underneath the panels; and the axletrees of the wheels were in the base: and the height of a wheel was a cubit and half a cubit.

units.leftText: The wheels were made like chariot wheels; their axles, rims, spokes, and hubs were all of cast metal.
units.rightText: And the work of the wheels was like the work of a chariot wheel: their axletrees, and their felloes, and their spokes, and their naves, were all molten.

units.leftText: Each stand had four handles, one for each corner, projecting from the stand.
units.rightText: And there were four undersetters at the four corners of each base: the undersetters thereof were of the base itself.

units.leftText: At the top of each stand was a circular band half a cubit high. The supports and panels were cast as a unit with the top of the stand.
units.rightText: And in the top of the base was there a round compass half a cubit high; and on the top of the base the stays thereof and the panels thereof were of the same.
leftNotes: 7:35 Half a cubit is approximately 9 inches or 22.9 centimeters high.

units.leftText: He engraved cherubim, lions, and palm trees on the surfaces of the supports and panels, wherever each had space, with wreaths all around.
units.rightText: And on the plates of the stays thereof, and on the panels thereof, he graved cherubim, lions, and palm-trees, according to the space of each, with wreaths round about.

units.leftText: In this way he made the ten stands, each with the same casting, dimensions, and shape. The Ten Bronze Basins (2 Chronicles 4:6–8|2CH 4:6-8*)
units.rightText: After this manner he made the ten bases: all of them had one casting, one measure, and one form.

units.leftText: He also made ten bronze basins, each holding forty baths and measuring four cubits across, one basin for each of the ten stands.
units.rightText: And he made ten lavers of brass: one laver contained forty baths; and every laver was four cubits; and upon every one of the ten bases one laver.
leftNotes: 7:38 40 baths is approximately 232 gallons or 880 liters.

units.leftText: He set five stands on the south side of the temple and five on the north, and he put the Sea on the south side, at the southeast corner of the temple. Completion of the Bronze Works (2 Chronicles 4:11–18|2CH 4:11-18*)
units.rightText: And he set the bases, five on the right side of the house, and five on the left side of the house: and he set the sea on the right side of the house eastward, toward the south.

units.leftText: Additionally, Huram made the pots, shovels, and sprinkling bowls. So Huram finished all the work that he had undertaken for King Solomon in the house of the LORD:
units.rightText: And Hiram made the lavers, and the shovels, and the basins. So Hiram made an end of doing all the work that he wrought for king Solomon in the house of Jehovah:
leftNotes: 7:40 Many Hebrew manuscripts, LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate (see also verse 45 and 2 Chronicles 4:11|2CH 4:11*); many other Hebrew manuscripts basins

units.leftText: the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals atop the pillars; the two sets of network covering both bowls of the capitals atop the pillars;
units.rightText: the two pillars, and the two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars; and the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars;

units.leftText: the four hundred pomegranates for the two sets of network (two rows of pomegranates for each network covering both the bowl-shaped capitals atop the pillars);
units.rightText: and the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks; two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were upon the pillars;

units.leftText: the ten stands; the ten basins on the stands;
units.rightText: and the ten bases, and the ten lavers on the bases;

units.leftText: the Sea; the twelve oxen underneath the Sea;
units.rightText: and the one sea, and the twelve oxen under the sea;

units.leftText: and the pots, shovels, and sprinkling bowls.
units.rightText: and the pots, and the shovels, and the basins: even all these vessels, which Hiram made for king Solomon, in the house of Jehovah, were of burnished brass.

units.leftText: The king had them cast in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan between Succoth and Zarethan.
units.rightText: In the plain of the Jordan did the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarethan.
leftNotes: 7:46 Zarethan is a variant of Zeredah; see 2 Chronicles 4:17|2CH 4:17*.

units.leftText: Solomon left all these articles unweighed, because there were so many. The weight of the bronze could not be determined. Completion of the Gold Furnishings (2 Chronicles 4:19–22|2CH 4:19-22*)
units.rightText: And Solomon left all the vessels unweighed, because they were exceeding many: the weight of the brass could not be found out.

units.leftText: Solomon also made all the furnishings for the house of the LORD: the golden altar; the golden table on which was placed the Bread of the Presence;
units.rightText: And Solomon made all the vessels that were in the house of Jehovah: the golden altar, and the table whereupon the showbread was, of gold;

units.leftText: the lampstands of pure gold in front of the inner sanctuary, five on the right side and five on the left; the gold flowers, lamps, and tongs;
units.rightText: and the candlesticks, five on the right side, and five on the left, before the oracle, of pure gold; and the flowers, and the lamps, and the tongs, of gold;

units.leftText: the pure gold basins, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, ladles, and censers; and the gold hinges for the doors of the inner temple (that is, the Most Holy Place ) as well as for the doors of the main hall of the temple.
units.rightText: and the cups, and the snuffers, and the basins, and the spoons, and the firepans, of pure gold; and the hinges, both for the doors of the inner house, the most holy place, and for the doors of the house, to wit, of the temple, of gold.
leftNotes: 7:50 Or the Holy of Holies

units.leftText: So all the work that King Solomon had performed for the house of the LORD was completed. Then Solomon brought in the items his father David had dedicated— the silver, the gold, and the furnishings— and he placed them in the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
units.rightText: Thus all the work that king Solomon wrought in the house of Jehovah was finished. And Solomon brought in the things which David his father had dedicated, even the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, and put them in the treasuries of the house of Jehovah.

units.leftText: At that time Solomon assembled before him in Jerusalem the elders of Israel — all the tribal heads and family leaders of the Israelites — to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Zion, the City of David.
units.rightText: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the princes of the fathers’ houses of the children of Israel, unto king Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of Jehovah out of the city of David, which is Zion.

units.leftText: And all the men of Israel came together to King Solomon at the feast in the seventh month, the month of Ethanim.
units.rightText: And all the men of Israel assembled themselves unto king Solomon at the feast, in the month Ethanim, which is the seventh month.
leftNotes: 8:2 That is, the Feast of Tabernacles (or Booths or Shelters); similarly in verse 65; see Leviticus 23:33–36|LEV 23:33-36*.
8:2 Ethanim was the seventh month of the ancient Hebrew lunar calendar, usually occurring within the months of September and October.

units.leftText: When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the priests took up the ark,
units.rightText: And all the elders of Israel came, and the priests took up the ark.

units.leftText: and they brought up the ark of the LORD and the Tent of Meeting with all its sacred furnishings. So the priests and Levites carried them up.
units.rightText: And they brought up the ark of Jehovah, and the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the Tent; even these did the priests and the Levites bring up.

units.leftText: There, before the ark, King Solomon and the whole congregation of Israel who had assembled with him sacrificed so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered.
units.rightText: And king Solomon and all the congregation of Israel, that were assembled unto him, were with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and oxen, that could not be counted nor numbered for multitude.

units.leftText: Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place in the inner sanctuary of the temple, the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
units.rightText: And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of Jehovah unto its place, into the oracle of the house, to the most holy place, even under the wings of the cherubim.
leftNotes: 8:6 Or the Holy of Holies

units.leftText: For the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark and overshadowed the ark and its poles.
units.rightText: For the cherubim spread forth their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and the staves thereof above.

units.leftText: The poles extended far enough that their ends were visible from the Holy Place in front of the inner sanctuary, but not from outside the Holy Place; and they are there to this day.
units.rightText: And the staves were so long that the ends of the staves were seen from the holy place before the oracle; but they were not seen without: and there they are unto this day.
leftNotes: 8:8 Literally not from outside

units.leftText: There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb, where the LORD had made a covenant with the Israelites after they had come out of the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: There was nothing in the ark save the two tables of stone which Moses put there at Horeb, when Jehovah made a covenant with the children of Israel, when they came out of the land of Egypt.
leftNotes: 8:9 That is, Mount Sinai, or possibly a mountain in the range containing Mount Sinai

units.leftText: And when the priests came out of the Holy Place, the cloud filled the house of the LORD
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the priests were come out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house of Jehovah,

units.leftText: so that the priests could not stand there to minister because of the cloud. For the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD. Solomon Blesses the LORD (2 Chronicles 6:1–11|2CH 6:1-11*)
units.rightText: so that the priests could not stand to minister by reason of the cloud; for the glory of Jehovah filled the house of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then Solomon declared: “The LORD has said that He would dwell in the thick cloud.
units.rightText: Then spake Solomon, Jehovah hath said that he would dwell in the thick darkness.
leftNotes: 8:12 Some LXX manuscripts The Lord has set the sun in the heavens, but

units.leftText: I have indeed built You an exalted house, a place for You to dwell forever.”
units.rightText: I have surely built thee a house of habitation, a place for thee to dwell in for ever.

units.leftText: And as the whole assembly of Israel stood there, the king turned around and blessed them all
units.rightText: And the king turned his face about, and blessed all the assembly of Israel: and all the assembly of Israel stood.

units.leftText: and said:
units.rightText: And he said, Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Israel, who spake with his mouth unto David my father, and hath with his hand fulfilled it, saying,

units.leftText: ‘Since the day I brought My people Israel out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city from any tribe of Israel in which to build a house so that My Name would be there. But I have chosen David to be over My people Israel.’
units.rightText: Since the day that I brought forth my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel to build a house, that my name might be there; but I chose David to be over my people Israel.

units.leftText: Now it was in the heart of my father David to build a house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: Now it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of Jehovah, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: But the LORD said to my father David, ‘Since it was in your heart to build a house for My Name, you have done well to have this in your heart.
units.rightText: But Jehovah said unto David my father, Whereas it was in thy heart to build a house for my name, thou didst well that it was in thy heart:

units.leftText: Nevertheless, you are not the one to build it; but your son, your own offspring, will build the house for My Name.’
units.rightText: nevertheless thou shalt not build the house; but thy son that shall come forth out of thy loins, he shall build the house for my name.

units.leftText: Now the LORD has fulfilled the word that He spoke. I have succeeded my father David, and I sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised. I have built the house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: And Jehovah hath established his word that he spake; for I am risen up in the room of David my father, and sit on the throne of Israel, as Jehovah promised, and have built the house for the name of Jehovah, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: And there I have provided a place for the ark, which contains the covenant of the LORD that He made with our fathers when He brought them out of the land of Egypt.” Solomon’s Prayer of Dedication (2 Chronicles 6:12–42|2CH 6:12-42*)
units.rightText: And there have I set a place for the ark, wherein is the covenant of Jehovah, which he made with our fathers, when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly of Israel, spread out his hands toward heaven,
units.rightText: And Solomon stood before the altar of Jehovah in the presence of all the assembly of Israel, and spread forth his hands toward heaven;

units.leftText: and said:
units.rightText: and he said, O Jehovah, the God of Israel, there is no God like thee, in heaven above, or on earth beneath; who keepest covenant and lovingkindness with thy servants, that walk before thee with all their heart;

units.leftText: You have kept Your promise to Your servant, my father David. What You spoke with Your mouth You have fulfilled with Your hand this day.
units.rightText: who hast kept with thy servant David my father that which thou didst promise him: yea, thou spakest with thy mouth, and hast fulfilled it with thy hand, as it is this day.

units.leftText: Therefore now, O LORD, God of Israel, keep for Your servant, my father David, what You promised when You said: ‘You will never fail to have a man to sit before Me on the throne of Israel, if only your descendants guard their way to walk before Me as you have done.’
units.rightText: Now therefore, O Jehovah, the God of Israel, keep with thy servant David my father that which thou hast promised him, saying, There shall not fail thee a man in my sight to sit on the throne of Israel, if only thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me as thou hast walked before me.

units.leftText: And now, O God of Israel, please confirm what You promised to Your servant, my father David.
units.rightText: Now therefore, O God of Israel, let thy word, I pray thee, be verified, which thou spakest unto thy servant David my father.

units.leftText: But will God indeed dwell upon the earth? The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You, much less this temple I have built.
units.rightText: But will God in very deed dwell on the earth? behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house that I have builded!

units.leftText: Yet regard the prayer and plea of Your servant, O LORD my God, so that You may hear the cry and the prayer that Your servant is praying before You today.
units.rightText: Yet have thou respect unto the prayer of thy servant, and to his supplication, O Jehovah my God, to hearken unto the cry and to the prayer which thy servant prayeth before thee this day;

units.leftText: May Your eyes be open toward this temple night and day, toward the place of which You said, ‘My Name shall be there,’ so that You may hear the prayer that Your servant prays toward this place.
units.rightText: that thine eyes may be open toward this house night and day, even toward the place whereof thou hast said, My name shall be there; to hearken unto the prayer which thy servant shall pray toward this place.

units.leftText: Hear the plea of Your servant and of Your people Israel when they pray toward this place. May You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place. May You hear and forgive.
units.rightText: And hearken thou to the supplication of thy servant, and of thy people Israel, when they shall pray toward this place: yea, hear thou in heaven thy dwelling-place; and when thou hearest, forgive.

units.leftText: When a man sins against his neighbor and is required to take an oath, and he comes to take an oath before Your altar in this temple,
units.rightText: If a man sin against his neighbor, and an oath be laid upon him to cause him to swear, and he come and swear before thine altar in this house;

units.leftText: then may You hear from heaven and act. May You judge Your servants, condemning the wicked man by bringing down on his own head what he has done, and justifying the righteous man by rewarding him according to his righteousness.
units.rightText: then hear thou in heaven, and do, and judge thy servants, condemning the wicked, to bring his way upon his own head, and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness.

units.leftText: When Your people Israel are defeated before an enemy because they have sinned against You, and they return to You and confess Your name, praying and pleading with You in this temple,
units.rightText: When thy people Israel are smitten down before the enemy, because they have sinned against thee; if they turn again to thee, and confess thy name, and pray and make supplication unto thee in this house:

units.leftText: then may You hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your people Israel. May You restore them to the land You gave to their fathers.
units.rightText: then hear thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of thy people Israel, and bring them again unto the land which thou gavest unto their fathers.

units.leftText: When the skies are shut and there is no rain because Your people have sinned against You, and they pray toward this place and confess Your name, and they turn from their sins because You have afflicted them,
units.rightText: When heaven is shut up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against thee; if they pray toward this place, and confess thy name, and turn from their sin, when thou dost afflict them:

units.leftText: then may You hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your servants, Your people Israel, so that You may teach them the good way in which they should walk. May You send rain on the land that You gave Your people as an inheritance.
units.rightText: then hear thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of thy servants, and of thy people Israel, when thou teachest them the good way wherein they should walk; and send rain upon thy land, which thou hast given to thy people for an inheritance.

units.leftText: When famine or plague comes upon the land, or blight or mildew or locusts or grasshoppers, or when their enemy besieges them in their cities, whatever plague or sickness may come,
units.rightText: If there be in the land famine, if there be pestilence, if there be blasting or mildew, locust or caterpillar; if their enemy besiege them in the land of their cities; whatsoever plague, whatsoever sickness there be;

units.leftText: then may whatever prayer or petition Your people Israel make— each knowing his own afflictions and spreading out his hands toward this temple—
units.rightText: what prayer and supplication soever be made by any man, or by all thy people Israel, who shall know every man the plague of his own heart, and spread forth his hands toward this house:

units.leftText: be heard by You from heaven, Your dwelling place. And may You forgive and act, and repay each man according to all his ways, since You know his heart — for You alone know the hearts of all men —
units.rightText: then hear thou in heaven thy dwelling-place, and forgive, and do, and render unto every man according to all his ways, whose heart thou knowest; (for thou, even thou only, knowest the hearts of all the children of men;)

units.leftText: so that they may fear You all the days they live in the land that You gave to our fathers.
units.rightText: that they may fear thee all the days that they live in the land which thou gavest unto our fathers.

units.leftText: And as for the foreigner who is not of Your people Israel but has come from a distant land because of Your name—
units.rightText: Moreover concerning the foreigner, that is not of thy people Israel, when he shall come out of a far country for thy name’s sake

units.leftText: for they will hear of Your great name and mighty hand and outstretched arm— when he comes and prays toward this temple,
units.rightText: (for they shall hear of thy great name, and of thy mighty hand, and of thine outstretched arm); when he shall come and pray toward this house;

units.leftText: then may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, and do according to all for which the foreigner calls to You. Then all the peoples of the earth will know Your name and fear You, as do Your people Israel, and they will know that this house I have built is called by Your Name.
units.rightText: hear thou in heaven thy dwelling-place, and do according to all that the foreigner calleth to thee for; that all the peoples of the earth may know thy name, to fear thee, as doth thy people Israel, and that they may know that this house which I have built is called by thy name.

units.leftText: When Your people go to war against their enemies, wherever You send them, and when they pray to the LORD in the direction of the city You have chosen and the house I have built for Your Name,
units.rightText: If thy people go out to battle against their enemy, by whatsoever way thou shalt send them, and they pray unto Jehovah toward the city which thou hast chosen, and toward the house which I have built for thy name;

units.leftText: then may You hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and may You uphold their cause.
units.rightText: then hear thou in heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.

units.leftText: When they sin against You — for there is no one who does not sin — and You become angry with them and deliver them to an enemy who takes them as captives to his own land, whether far or near,
units.rightText: If they sin against thee (for there is no man that sinneth not), and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captive unto the land of the enemy, far off or near;

units.leftText: and when they come to their senses in the land to which they were taken, and they repent and plead with You in the land of their captors, saying, ‘We have sinned and done wrong; we have acted wickedly,’
units.rightText: yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they are carried captive, and turn again, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captive, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have dealt wickedly;

units.leftText: and when they return to You with all their heart and soul in the land of the enemies who took them captive, and when they pray to You in the direction of the land that You gave to their fathers, the city You have chosen, and the house I have built for Your Name,
units.rightText: if they return unto thee with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their enemies, who carried them captive, and pray unto thee toward their land, which thou gavest unto their fathers, the city which thou hast chosen, and the house which I have built for thy name:

units.leftText: then may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, their prayer and petition, and may You uphold their cause.
units.rightText: then hear thou their prayer and their supplication in heaven thy dwelling-place, and maintain their cause;

units.leftText: May You forgive Your people who have sinned against You and all the transgressions they have committed against You, and may You grant them compassion in the eyes of their captors to show them mercy.
units.rightText: and forgive thy people who have sinned against thee, and all their transgressions wherein they have transgressed against thee; and give them compassion before those who carried them captive, that they may have compassion on them

units.leftText: For they are Your people and Your inheritance; You brought them out of Egypt, out of the furnace for iron.
units.rightText: (for they are thy people, and thine inheritance, which thou broughtest forth out of Egypt, from the midst of the furnace of iron);

units.leftText: May Your eyes be open to the pleas of Your servant and of Your people Israel, and may You listen to them whenever they call to You.
units.rightText: that thine eyes may be open unto the supplication of thy servant, and unto the supplication of thy people Israel, to hearken unto them whensoever they cry unto thee.

units.leftText: For You, O Lord GOD, have set them apart from all the peoples of the earth as Your inheritance, as You spoke through Your servant Moses when You brought our fathers out of Egypt.” Solomon’s Benediction
units.rightText: For thou didst separate them from among all the peoples of the earth, to be thine inheritance, as thou spakest by Moses thy servant, when thou broughtest our fathers out of Egypt, O Lord Jehovah.

units.leftText: Now when Solomon had finished praying this entire prayer and petition to the LORD, he got up before the altar of the LORD, where he had been kneeling with his hands spread out toward heaven.
units.rightText: And it was so, that, when Solomon had made an end of praying all this prayer and supplication unto Jehovah, he arose from before the altar of Jehovah, from kneeling on his knees with his hands spread forth toward heaven.

units.leftText: And he stood and blessed the whole assembly of Israel in a loud voice, saying:
units.rightText: And he stood, and blessed all the assembly of Israel with a loud voice, saying,

units.leftText: “Blessed be the LORD, who has given rest to His people Israel according to all that He promised. Not one word has failed of all the good promises He made through His servant Moses.
units.rightText: Blessed be Jehovah, that hath given rest unto his people Israel, according to all that he promised: there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by Moses his servant.

units.leftText: May the LORD our God be with us, as He was with our fathers. May He never leave us or forsake us.
units.rightText: Jehovah our God be with us, as he was with our fathers: let him not leave us, nor forsake us;

units.leftText: May He incline our hearts to Himself, to walk in all His ways and to keep the commandments and statutes and ordinances He commanded our fathers.
units.rightText: that he may incline our hearts unto him, to walk in all his ways, and to keep his commandments, and his statutes, and his ordinances, which he commanded our fathers.

units.leftText: And may these words with which I have made my petition before the LORD be near to the LORD our God day and night, so that He may uphold the cause of His servant and of His people Israel as each day requires,
units.rightText: And let these my words, wherewith I have made supplication before Jehovah, be nigh unto Jehovah our God day and night, that he maintain the cause of his servant, and the cause of his people Israel, as every day shall require;

units.leftText: so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God. There is no other!
units.rightText: that all the peoples of the earth may know that Jehovah, he is God; there is none else.

units.leftText: So let your heart be fully devoted to the LORD our God, as it is this day, to walk in His statutes and to keep His commandments.” Sacrifices of Dedication (2 Chronicles 7:4–10|2CH 7:4-10*)
units.rightText: Let your heart therefore be perfect with Jehovah our God, to walk in his statutes, and to keep his commandments, as at this day.

units.leftText: Then the king and all Israel with him offered sacrifices before the LORD.
units.rightText: And the king, and all Israel with him, offered sacrifice before Jehovah.

units.leftText: And Solomon offered as peace offerings to the LORD 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep. So the king and all the Israelites dedicated the house of the LORD.
units.rightText: And Solomon offered for the sacrifice of peace-offerings, which he offered unto Jehovah, two and twenty thousand oxen, and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the children of Israel dedicated the house of Jehovah.

units.leftText: On that same day the king consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD, and there he offered the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings, since the bronze altar before the LORD was too small to contain all these offerings.
units.rightText: The same day did the king hallow the middle of the court that was before the house of Jehovah; for there he offered the burnt-offering, and the meal-offering, and the fat of the peace-offerings, because the brazen altar that was before Jehovah was too little to receive the burnt-offering, and the meal-offering, and the fat of the peace-offerings.

units.leftText: So at that time Solomon and all Israel with him— a great assembly of people from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt— kept the feast before the LORD our God for seven days and seven more days— fourteen days in all.
units.rightText: So Solomon held the feast at that time, and all Israel with him, a great assembly, from the entrance of Hamath unto the brook of Egypt, before Jehovah our God, seven days and seven days, even fourteen days.

units.leftText: On the fifteenth day Solomon sent the people away. So they blessed the king and went home, joyful and glad in heart for all the good things that the LORD had done for His servant David and for His people Israel.
units.rightText: On the eighth day he sent the people away; and they blessed the king, and went unto their tents joyful and glad of heart for all the goodness that Jehovah had showed unto David his servant, and to Israel his people.
leftNotes: 8:66 Hebrew On the eighth day, probably referring to the day following the seven-day feast; see 2 Chronicles 7:9–10|2CH 7:9-10*.

units.leftText: Now when Solomon had finished building the house of the LORD and the royal palace, and had achieved all that he had desired to do,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Solomon had finished the building of the house of Jehovah, and the king’s house, and all Solomon’s desire which he was pleased to do,

units.leftText: the LORD appeared to him a second time, as He had appeared to him at Gibeon.
units.rightText: that Jehovah appeared to Solomon the second time, as he had appeared unto him at Gibeon.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to him: “I have heard your prayer and petition before Me. I have consecrated this temple, which you have built, by putting My Name there forever; My eyes and My heart will be there for all time.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto him, I have heard thy prayer and thy supplication, that thou hast made before me: I have hallowed this house, which thou hast built, to put my name there for ever; and mine eyes and my heart shall be there perpetually.

units.leftText: And as for you, if you walk before Me as your father David walked, with a heart of integrity and uprightness, doing all I have commanded you, and if you keep My statutes and ordinances,
units.rightText: And as for thee, if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked, in integrity of heart, and in uprightness, to do according to all that I have commanded thee, and wilt keep my statutes and mine ordinances;

units.leftText: then I will establish your royal throne over Israel forever, as I promised your father David when I said, ‘You will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel.’
units.rightText: then I will establish the throne of thy kingdom over Israel for ever, according as I promised to David thy father, saying, There shall not fail thee a man upon the throne of Israel.

units.leftText: But if indeed you or your sons turn away from following Me and do not keep the commandments and statutes I have set before you, and if you go off to serve and worship other gods,
units.rightText: But if ye shall turn away from following me, ye or your children, and not keep my commandments and my statutes which I have set before you, but shall go and serve other gods, and worship them;

units.leftText: then I will cut off Israel from the land that I have given them, and I will banish from My presence this temple I have sanctified for My Name. Then Israel will become an object of scorn and ridicule among all peoples.
units.rightText: then will I cut off Israel out of the land which I have given them; and this house, which I have hallowed for my name, will I cast out of my sight; and Israel shall be a proverb and a byword among all peoples.

units.leftText: And when this temple has become a heap of rubble, all who pass by it will be appalled and will hiss and say, ‘Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?’
units.rightText: And though this house is so high, yet shall every one that passeth by it be astonished, and shall hiss; and they shall say, Why hath Jehovah done thus unto this land, and to this house?
leftNotes: 9:8 Some LXX manuscripts, Syriac, and Arabic; Hebrew And though this temple is now exalted; see also 2 Chronicles 7:21|2CH 7:21*.

units.leftText: And others will answer, ‘Because they have forsaken the LORD their God who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and have embraced other gods, worshiping and serving them— because of this, the LORD has brought all this disaster upon them.’” Solomon’s Additional Achievements (2 Chronicles 8:1–18|2CH 8:1-18*)
units.rightText: and they shall answer, Because they forsook Jehovah their God, who brought forth their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and laid hold on other gods, and worshipped them, and served them: therefore hath Jehovah brought all this evil upon them.

units.leftText: Now at the end of the twenty years during which Solomon built these two houses, the house of the LORD and the royal palace,
units.rightText: And it came to pass at the end of twenty years, wherein Solomon had built the two houses, the house of Jehovah and the king’s house

units.leftText: King Solomon gave twenty towns in the land of Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre, who had supplied him with cedar and cypress logs and gold for his every desire.
units.rightText: (now Hiram the king of Tyre had furnished Solomon with cedar-trees and fir-trees, and with gold, according to all his desire), that then king Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.
leftNotes: 9:11 Or pine or juniper or fir

units.leftText: So Hiram went out from Tyre to inspect the towns that Solomon had given him, but he was not pleased with them.
units.rightText: And Hiram came out from Tyre to see the cities which Solomon had given him; and they pleased him not.

units.leftText: “What are these towns you have given me, my brother?” asked Hiram, and he called them the Land of Cabul, as they are called to this day.
units.rightText: And he said, What cities are these which thou hast given me, my brother? And he called them the land of Cabul unto this day.
leftNotes: 9:13 Cabul sounds like the Hebrew for good-for-nothing.

units.leftText: And Hiram had sent the king 120 talents of gold.
units.rightText: And Hiram sent to the king sixscore talents of gold.
leftNotes: 9:14 120 talents is approximately 4.52 tons or 4.1 metric tons of gold.

units.leftText: This is the account of the forced labor that King Solomon imposed to build the house of the LORD, his own palace, the supporting terraces, and the wall of Jerusalem, as well as Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
units.rightText: And this is the reason of the levy which king Solomon raised, to build the house of Jehovah, and his own house, and Millo, and the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor, and Megiddo, and Gezer.
leftNotes: 9:15 Hebrew the Millo; also in verse 24

units.leftText: Pharaoh king of Egypt had attacked and captured Gezer. He had set it on fire, killed the Canaanites who lived in the city, and given it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon’s wife.
units.rightText: Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up, and taken Gezer, and burnt it with fire, and slain the Canaanites that dwelt in the city, and given it for a portion unto his daughter, Solomon’s wife.

units.leftText: So Solomon rebuilt Gezer, Lower Beth-horon,
units.rightText: And Solomon built Gezer, and Beth-horon the nether,

units.leftText: Baalath, and Tamar in the Wilderness of Judah,
units.rightText: and Baalath, and Tamar in the wilderness, in the land,
leftNotes: 9:18 Alternate MT reading; the other alternate reads Tadmor
9:18 Hebrew in the wilderness in the land

units.leftText: as well as all the store cities that Solomon had for his chariots and horses — whatever he desired to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and throughout the land of his dominion.
units.rightText: and all the store-cities that Solomon had, and the cities for his chariots, and the cities for his horsemen, and that which Solomon desired to build for his pleasure in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.
leftNotes: 9:19 Or horsemen or charioteers

units.leftText: As for all the people who remained of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites (the people who were not Israelites) —
units.rightText: As for all the people that were left of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who were not of the children of Israel;

units.leftText: their descendants who remained in the land, those whom the Israelites were unable to devote to destruction — Solomon conscripted these people to be forced laborers, as they are to this day.
units.rightText: their children that were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel were not able utterly to destroy, of them did Solomon raise a levy of bondservants unto this day.
leftNotes: 9:21 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering.

units.leftText: But Solomon did not consign any of the Israelites to slavery, because they were his men of war, his servants, his officers, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry.
units.rightText: But of the children of Israel did Solomon make no bondservants; but they were the men of war, and his servants, and his princes, and his captains, and rulers of his chariots and of his horsemen.

units.leftText: They were also the chief officers over Solomon’s projects: 550 supervisors over the people who did the work.
units.rightText: These were the chief officers that were over Solomon’s work, five hundred and fifty, who bare rule over the people that wrought in the work.

units.leftText: As soon as Pharaoh’s daughter had come up from the City of David to the palace that Solomon had built for her, he built the supporting terraces.
units.rightText: But Pharaoh’s daughter came up out of the city of David unto her house which Solomon had built for her: then did he build Millo.

units.leftText: Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he had built for the LORD, burning incense with them before the LORD. So he completed the temple.
units.rightText: And three times in a year did Solomon offer burnt-offerings and peace-offerings upon the altar which he built unto Jehovah, burning incense therewith, upon the altar that was before Jehovah. So he finished the house.

units.leftText: King Solomon also assembled a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, which is near Eloth in Edom, on the shore of the Red Sea.
units.rightText: And king Solomon made a navy of ships in Ezion-geber, which is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red Sea, in the land of Edom.
leftNotes: 9:26 Eloth is a variant of Elath; see LXX, 2 Kings 14:22|2KI 14:22*, and 2 Kings 16:6.
9:26 Or the Sea of Reeds

units.leftText: And Hiram sent his servants, sailors who knew the sea, to serve in the fleet with Solomon’s servants.
units.rightText: And Hiram sent in the navy his servants, shipmen that had knowledge of the sea, with the servants of Solomon.

units.leftText: They sailed to Ophir and imported gold from there— 420 talents — and delivered it to Solomon.
units.rightText: And they came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and brought it to king Solomon.
leftNotes: 9:28 420 talents is approximately 15.8 tons or 14.4 metric tons of gold.

units.leftText: Now when the queen of Sheba heard about the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to test him with difficult questions.
units.rightText: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of Jehovah, she came to prove him with hard questions.

units.leftText: She arrived in Jerusalem with a very large caravan— with camels bearing spices, gold in great abundance, and precious stones.
units.rightText: And she came to Jerusalem with a very great train, with camels that bare spices, and very much gold, and precious stones; and when she was come to Solomon, she communed with him of all that was in her heart.

units.leftText: And Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too difficult for the king to explain.
units.rightText: And Solomon told her all her questions: there was not anything hid from the king which he told her not.

units.leftText: When the queen of Sheba saw all the wisdom of Solomon, the palace he had built,
units.rightText: And when the queen of Sheba had seen all the wisdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built,

units.leftText: the food at his table, the seating of his servants, the service and attire of his attendants, his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he presented at the house of the LORD, it took her breath away.
units.rightText: and the food of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel, and his cupbearers, and his ascent by which he went up unto the house of Jehovah; there was no more spirit in her.

units.leftText: She said to the king, “The report I heard in my own country about your words and wisdom is true.
units.rightText: And she said to the king, It was a true report that I heard in mine own land of thine acts, and of thy wisdom.

units.leftText: But I did not believe these things until I came and saw with my own eyes. Indeed, not even half was told to me. Your wisdom and prosperity have far exceeded the report I heard.
units.rightText: Howbeit I believed not the words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen it: and, behold, the half was not told me; thy wisdom and prosperity exceed the fame which I heard.

units.leftText: How blessed are your men! How blessed are these servants of yours who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!
units.rightText: Happy are thy men, happy are these thy servants, that stand continually before thee, and that hear thy wisdom.
leftNotes: 10:8 LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate your wives

units.leftText: Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you to set you on the throne of Israel. Because of the LORD’s eternal love for Israel, He has made you king to carry out justice and righteousness.”
units.rightText: Blessed be Jehovah thy God, who delighted in thee, to set thee on the throne of Israel: because Jehovah loved Israel for ever, therefore made he thee king, to do justice and righteousness.

units.leftText: Then she gave the king 120 talents of gold, a great quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never again were spices in such abundance brought in as those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
units.rightText: And she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and of spices very great store, and precious stones: there came no more such abundance of spices as these which the queen of Sheba gave to king Solomon.
leftNotes: 10:10 120 talents is approximately 4.52 tons or 4.1 metric tons of gold.

units.leftText: (The fleet of Hiram that brought gold from Ophir also brought from Ophir a great cargo of almug wood and precious stones.
units.rightText: And the navy also of Hiram, that brought gold from Ophir, brought in from Ophir great plenty of almug-trees and precious stones.
leftNotes: 10:11 Almug is probably a variant of algum; also in verse 12; see 2 Chronicles 2:8|2CH 2:8*.

units.leftText: The king made the almug wood into steps for the house of the LORD and for the king’s palace, and into lyres and harps for the singers. Never before had such almug wood been brought in, nor has such been seen again to this day.)
units.rightText: And the king made of the almug-trees pillars for the house of Jehovah, and for the king’s house, harps also and psalteries for the singers: there came no such almug-trees, nor were seen, unto this day.

units.leftText: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all she desired — whatever she asked — besides what he had given her out of his royal bounty. Then she left and returned to her own country, along with her servants. Solomon’s Wealth and Splendor (2 Chronicles 1:14–17|2CH 1:14-17*; 2 Chronicles 9:13–28|2CH 9:13-28*)
units.rightText: And king Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatsoever she asked, besides that which Solomon gave her of his royal bounty. So she turned, and went to her own land, she and her servants.

units.leftText: The weight of gold that came to Solomon each year was 666 talents,
units.rightText: Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred threescore and six talents of gold,
leftNotes: 10:14 666 talents is approximately 25.1 tons or 22.8 metric tons of gold.

units.leftText: not including the revenue from the merchants, traders, and all the Arabian kings and governors of the land.
units.rightText: besides that which the traders brought, and the traffic of the merchants, and of all the kings of the mingled people, and of the governors of the country.

units.leftText: King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; six hundred shekels of gold went into each shield.
units.rightText: And king Solomon made two hundred bucklers of beaten gold; six hundred shekels of gold went to one buckler.
leftNotes: 10:16 600 shekels is approximately 15.1 pounds or 6.8 kilograms of gold.

units.leftText: He also made three hundred small shields of hammered gold; three minas of gold went into each shield. And the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
units.rightText: And he made three hundred shields of beaten gold; three pounds of gold went to one shield: and the king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.
leftNotes: 10:17 3 minas is approximately 3.77 pounds or 1.71 kilograms of gold; possibly a reference to double minas, that is, approximately 7.54 pounds or 3.42 kilograms.

units.leftText: Additionally, the king made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with pure gold.
units.rightText: Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with the finest gold.

units.leftText: The throne had six steps, and its back had a rounded top. There were armrests on both sides of the seat, with a lion standing beside each armrest.
units.rightText: There were six steps to the throne, and the top of the throne was round behind; and there were stays on either side by the place of the seat, and two lions standing beside the stays.

units.leftText: Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at either end of each step. Nothing like this had ever been made for any kingdom.
units.rightText: And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps: there was not the like made in any kingdom.

units.leftText: All King Solomon’s drinking cups were gold, and all the utensils of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. There was no silver, because it was accounted as nothing in the days of Solomon.
units.rightText: And all king Solomon’s drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were of pure gold: none were of silver; it was nothing accounted of in the days of Solomon.

units.leftText: For the king had the ships of Tarshish at sea with Hiram’s fleet, and once every three years the ships of Tarshish would arrive bearing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
units.rightText: For the king had at sea a navy of Tarshish with the navy of Hiram: once every three years came the navy of Tarshish, bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.
leftNotes: 10:22 Or a fleet of trading ships; twice in this verse
10:22 Or baboons

units.leftText: So King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
units.rightText: So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.

units.leftText: The whole world sought an audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart.
units.rightText: And all the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.

units.leftText: Year after year, each visitor would bring his tribute: articles of silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
units.rightText: And they brought every man his tribute, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and raiment, and armor, and spices, horses, and mules, a rate year by year.

units.leftText: Solomon accumulated 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses, which he stationed in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And Solomon gathered together chariots and horsemen: and he had a thousand and four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, that he bestowed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem.
leftNotes: 10:26 Literally Solomon accumulated chariots and horses; he had
10:26 Or horsemen or charioteers

units.leftText: The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as abundant as sycamore in the foothills.
units.rightText: And the king made silver to be in Jerusalem as stones, and cedars made he to be as the sycomore-trees that are in the lowland, for abundance.
leftNotes: 10:27 Hebrew Shephelah or lowlands; that is, the western foothills of Judea

units.leftText: Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and Kue; the royal merchants purchased them from Kue.
units.rightText: And the horses which Solomon had were brought out of Egypt; and the king’s merchants received them in droves, each drove at a price.
leftNotes: 10:28 Probably an area in Cilicia, a province in the southeast of Asia Minor

units.leftText: A chariot could be imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. Likewise, they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram.
units.rightText: And a chariot came up and went out of Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty; and so for all the kings of the Hittites, and for the kings of Syria, did they bring them out by their means.
leftNotes: 10:29 600 shekels is approximately 15.1 pounds or 6.8 kilograms of silver.
10:29 150 shekels is approximately 3.8 pounds or 1.7 kilograms of silver.

units.leftText: King Solomon, however, loved many foreign women along with the daughter of Pharaoh — women of Moab, Ammon, Edom, and Sidon, as well as Hittite women.
units.rightText: Now king Solomon loved many foreign women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians, and Hittites;

units.leftText: These women were from the nations about which the LORD had told the Israelites, “You must not intermarry with them, for surely they will turn your hearts after their gods.” Yet Solomon clung to these women in love.
units.rightText: of the nations concerning which Jehovah said unto the children of Israel, Ye shall not go among them, neither shall they come among you; for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods: Solomon clave unto these in love.

units.leftText: He had seven hundred wives of royal birth and three hundred concubines — and his wives turned his heart away.
units.rightText: And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines; and his wives turned away his heart.

units.leftText: For when Solomon grew old, his wives turned his heart after other gods, and he was not wholeheartedly devoted to the LORD his God, as his father David had been.
units.rightText: For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods; and his heart was not perfect with Jehovah his God, as was the heart of David his father.

units.leftText: Solomon followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
units.rightText: For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
leftNotes: 11:5 Milcom is a variant of Molech; also in verse 33; see verse 7 and Leviticus 18:21|LEV 18:21*.

units.leftText: So Solomon did evil in the sight of the LORD; unlike his father David, he did not follow the LORD completely.
units.rightText: And Solomon did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah, and went not fully after Jehovah, as did David his father.

units.leftText: At that time on a hill east of Jerusalem, Solomon built a high place for Chemosh the abomination of Moab and for Molech the abomination of the Ammonites.
units.rightText: Then did Solomon build a high place for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, in the mount that is before Jerusalem, and for Molech the abomination of the children of Ammon.

units.leftText: He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods. God’s Anger against Solomon
units.rightText: And so did he for all his foreign wives, who burnt incense and sacrificed unto their gods.

units.leftText: Now the LORD grew angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice.
units.rightText: And Jehovah was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned away from Jehovah, the God of Israel, who had appeared unto him twice,

units.leftText: Although He had warned Solomon explicitly not to follow other gods, Solomon did not keep the LORD’s command.
units.rightText: and had commanded him concerning this thing, that he should not go after other gods: but he kept not that which Jehovah commanded.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Solomon, “Because you have done this and have not kept My covenant and My statutes, which I have commanded you, I will tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.
units.rightText: Wherefore Jehovah said unto Solomon, Forasmuch as this is done of thee, and thou hast not kept my covenant and my statutes, which I have commanded thee, I will surely rend the kingdom from thee, and will give it to thy servant.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, for the sake of your father David, I will not do it during your lifetime; I will tear it out of the hand of your son.
units.rightText: Notwithstanding in thy days I will not do it, for David thy father’s sake: but I will rend it out of the hand of thy son.

units.leftText: Yet I will not tear the whole kingdom away from him. I will give one tribe to your son for the sake of My servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen.” Hadad’s Return
units.rightText: Howbeit I will not rend away all the kingdom; but I will give one tribe to thy son, for David my servant’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake which I have chosen.

units.leftText: Then the LORD raised up against Solomon an adversary, Hadad the Edomite, from the royal line of Edom.
units.rightText: And Jehovah raised up an adversary unto Solomon, Hadad the Edomite: he was of the king’s seed in Edom.

units.leftText: Earlier, when David was in Edom, Joab the commander of the army had gone to bury the dead and had struck down every male in Edom.
units.rightText: For it came to pass, when David was in Edom, and Joab the captain of the host was gone up to bury the slain, and had smitten every male in Edom

units.leftText: Joab and all Israel had stayed there six months, until he had killed every male in Edom.
units.rightText: (for Joab and all Israel remained there six months, until he had cut off every male in Edom);

units.leftText: But Hadad, still just a young boy, had fled to Egypt, along with some Edomites who were servants of his father.
units.rightText: that Hadad fled, he and certain Edomites of his father’s servants with him, to go into Egypt, Hadad being yet a little child.

units.leftText: Hadad and his men set out from Midian and went to Paran. They took men from Paran with them and went to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave Hadad a house and land and provided him with food.
units.rightText: And they arose out of Midian, and came to Paran; and they took men with them out of Paran, and they came to Egypt, unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave him a house, and appointed him victuals, and gave him land.

units.leftText: There Hadad found such great favor in the sight of Pharaoh that he gave to him in marriage the sister of Queen Tahpenes, his own wife.
units.rightText: And Hadad found great favor in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him to wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.

units.leftText: And the sister of Tahpenes bore Hadad a son named Genubath. Tahpenes herself weaned him in Pharaoh’s palace, and Genubath lived there among the sons of Pharaoh.
units.rightText: And the sister of Tahpenes bare him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh’s house; and Genubath was in Pharaoh’s house among the sons of Pharaoh.

units.leftText: When Hadad heard in Egypt that David had rested with his fathers and that Joab, the commander of the army, was dead, he said to Pharaoh, “Let me go, that I may return to my own country.”
units.rightText: And when Hadad heard in Egypt that David slept with his fathers, and that Joab the captain of the host was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, Let me depart, that I may go to mine own country.

units.leftText: But Pharaoh asked him, “What have you lacked here with me that you suddenly want to go back to your own country?” “Nothing,” Hadad replied, “but please let me go.” Rezon’s Hostility
units.rightText: Then Pharaoh said unto him, But what hast thou lacked with me, that, behold, thou seekest to go to thine own country? And he answered, Nothing: howbeit only let me depart.

units.leftText: And God raised up against Solomon another adversary, Rezon the son of Eliada, who had fled from his master, Hadadezer king of Zobah,
units.rightText: And God raised up another adversary unto him, Rezon the son of Eliada, who had fled from his lord Hadadezer king of Zobah.

units.leftText: and had gathered men to himself. When David killed the Zobaites, Rezon captained a band of raiders and went to Damascus, where they settled and gained control.
units.rightText: And he gathered men unto him, and became captain over a troop, when David slew them of Zobah: and they went to Damascus, and dwelt therein, and reigned in Damascus.

units.leftText: Rezon was Israel’s enemy throughout the days of Solomon, adding to the trouble caused by Hadad. So Rezon ruled over Aram with hostility toward Israel. Jeroboam’s Rebellion
units.rightText: And he was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, besides the mischief that Hadad did: and he abhorred Israel, and reigned over Syria.

units.leftText: Now Jeroboam son of Nebat was an Ephraimite from Zeredah whose mother was a widow named Zeruah. Jeroboam was a servant of Solomon, but he rebelled against the king,
units.rightText: And Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephraimite of Zeredah, a servant of Solomon, whose mother’s name was Zeruah, a widow, he also lifted up his hand against the king.

units.leftText: and this is the account of his rebellion against the king.
units.rightText: And this was the reason why he lifted up his hand against the king: Solomon built Millo, and repaired the breach of the city of David his father.

units.leftText: Now Jeroboam was a mighty man of valor. So when Solomon noticed that the young man was industrious, he put him in charge of the whole labor force of the house of Joseph.
units.rightText: And the man Jeroboam was a mighty man of valor; and Solomon saw the young man that he was industrious, and he gave him charge over all the labor of the house of Joseph.

units.leftText: During that time, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met Jeroboam on the road as he was going out of Jerusalem. Now Ahijah had wrapped himself in a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the open field.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at that time, when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, that the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him in the way; now Ahijah had clad himself with a new garment; and they two were alone in the field.

units.leftText: And Ahijah took hold of the new cloak he was wearing, tore it into twelve pieces,
units.rightText: And Ahijah laid hold of the new garment that was on him, and rent it in twelve pieces.

units.leftText: and said to Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces for yourself, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Behold, I will tear the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and I will give you ten tribes.
units.rightText: And he said to Jeroboam, Take thee ten pieces; for thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee

units.leftText: But one tribe will remain for the sake of My servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel.
units.rightText: (but he shall have one tribe, for my servant David’s sake and for Jerusalem’s sake, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel);

units.leftText: For they have forsaken Me to worship Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites. They have not walked in My ways, nor done what is right in My eyes, nor kept My statutes and judgments, as Solomon’s father David did.
units.rightText: because that they have forsaken me, and have worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon; and they have not walked in my ways, to do that which is right in mine eyes, and to keep my statutes and mine ordinances, as did David his father.
leftNotes: 11:33 Hebrew; LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate he has; twice in this verse

units.leftText: Nevertheless, I will not take the whole kingdom out of Solomon’s hand, because I have made him ruler all the days of his life for the sake of David My servant, whom I chose because he kept My commandments and statutes.
units.rightText: Howbeit I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand; but I will make him prince all the days of his life, for David my servant’s sake whom I chose, who kept my commandments and my statutes;

units.leftText: But I will take ten tribes of the kingdom from the hand of his son and give them to you.
units.rightText: but I will take the kingdom out of his son’s hand, and will give it unto thee, even ten tribes.

units.leftText: I will give one tribe to his son, so that My servant David will always have a lamp before Me in Jerusalem, the city where I chose to put My Name.
units.rightText: And unto his son will I give one tribe, that David my servant may have a lamp alway before me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen me to put my name there.

units.leftText: But as for you, I will take you, and you shall reign over all that your heart desires, and you will be king over Israel.
units.rightText: And I will take thee, and thou shalt reign according to all that thy soul desireth, and shalt be king over Israel.

units.leftText: If you listen to all that I command you, walk in My ways, and do what is right in My sight in order to keep My statutes and commandments as My servant David did, then I will be with you. I will build you a lasting dynasty just as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.
units.rightText: And it shall be, if thou wilt hearken unto all that I command thee, and wilt walk in my ways, and do that which is right in mine eyes, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did; that I will be with thee, and will build thee a sure house, as I built for David, and will give Israel unto thee.

units.leftText: Because of this, I will humble David’s descendants — but not forever.’”
units.rightText: And I will for this afflict the seed of David, but not for ever.

units.leftText: Solomon therefore sought to kill Jeroboam. But Jeroboam arose and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, where he remained until the death of Solomon. The Death of Solomon (2 Chronicles 9:29–31|2CH 9:29-31*)
units.rightText: Solomon sought therefore to kill Jeroboam; but Jeroboam arose, and fled into Egypt, unto Shishak king of Egypt, and was in Egypt until the death of Solomon.

units.leftText: As for the rest of the acts of Solomon — all that he did, as well as his wisdom — are they not written in the Book of the Acts of Solomon?
units.rightText: Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon?

units.leftText: Thus the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
units.rightText: And the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.

units.leftText: And Solomon rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of his father David. And his son Rehoboam reigned in his place.
units.rightText: And Solomon slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David his father: and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: Then Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had gone there to make him king.
units.rightText: And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king.

units.leftText: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about this, he was still in Egypt where he had fled from King Solomon and had been living ever since.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard of it (for he was yet in Egypt, whither he had fled from the presence of king Solomon, and Jeroboam dwelt in Egypt,
leftNotes: 12:2 Or he remained

units.leftText: So they sent for Jeroboam, and he and the whole assembly of Israel came to Rehoboam and said,
units.rightText: and they sent and called him), that Jeroboam and all the assembly of Israel came, and spake unto Rehoboam, saying,

units.leftText: “Your father put a heavy yoke on us. But now you must lighten the burden of your father’s service and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you.”
units.rightText: Thy father made our yoke grievous: now therefore make thou the grievous service of thy father, and his heavy yoke which he put upon us, lighter, and we will serve thee.

units.leftText: Rehoboam answered, “Go away for three days and then return to me.” So the people departed.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Depart yet for three days, then come again to me. And the people departed.

units.leftText: Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. “How do you advise me to respond to these people?” he asked.
units.rightText: And king Rehoboam took counsel with the old men, that had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, What counsel give ye me to return answer to this people?

units.leftText: They replied, “If you will be a servant to these people and serve them this day, and if you will respond by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.”
units.rightText: And they spake unto him, saying, If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.

units.leftText: But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders; instead, he consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served him.
units.rightText: But he forsook the counsel of the old men which they had given him, and took counsel with the young men that were grown up with him, that stood before him.

units.leftText: He asked them, “What message do you advise that we send back to these people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, What counsel give ye, that we may return answer to this people, who have spoken to me, saying, Make the yoke that thy father did put upon us lighter?

units.leftText: The young men who had grown up with him replied, “This is how you should answer these people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you must make it lighter.’ This is what you should tell them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!
units.rightText: And the young men that were grown up with him spake unto him, saying, Thus shalt thou say unto this people that spake unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou it lighter unto us; thus shalt thou speak unto them, My little finger is thicker than my father’s loins.

units.leftText: Whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.’”
units.rightText: And now whereas my father did lade you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.

units.leftText: After three days, Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, since the king had said, “Come back to me on the third day.”
units.rightText: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam the third day, as the king bade, saying, Come to me again the third day.

units.leftText: And the king answered the people harshly. He rejected the advice of the elders
units.rightText: And the king answered the people roughly, and forsook the counsel of the old men which they had given him,

units.leftText: and spoke to them as the young men had advised, saying, “Whereas my father made your yoke heavy, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.”
units.rightText: and spake to them after the counsel of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.

units.leftText: So the king did not listen to the people, and indeed this turn of events was from the LORD, to fulfill the word He had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah the Shilonite. The Kingdom Divided (2 Chronicles 10:16–19|2CH 10:16-19*)
units.rightText: So the king hearkened not unto the people; for it was a thing brought about of Jehovah, that he might establish his word, which Jehovah spake by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

units.leftText: When all Israel saw that the king had refused to listen to them, they answered the king: “What portion do we have in David, and what inheritance in the son of Jesse? To your tents, O Israel! Look now to your own house, O David!”
units.rightText: And when all Israel saw that the king hearkened not unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David. So Israel departed unto their tents.

units.leftText: but Rehoboam still reigned over the Israelites living in the cities of Judah.
units.rightText: But as for the children of Israel that dwelt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.

units.leftText: Then King Rehoboam sent out Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, but all Israel stoned him to death. And King Rehoboam mounted his chariot in haste and escaped to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Then king Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the men subject to taskwork; and all Israel stoned him to death with stones. And king Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem.
leftNotes: 12:18 Hebrew; some LXX manuscripts and Syriac Adoniram; see 1 Kings 4:6|1KI 4:6* and 1 Kings 5:14.

units.leftText: So to this day Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David. Shemaiah’s Prophecy (2 Chronicles 11:1–4|2CH 11:1-4*)
units.rightText: So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.

units.leftText: When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, they summoned him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel. Only the tribe of Judah followed the house of David.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when all Israel heard that Jeroboam was returned, that they sent and called him unto the congregation, and made him king over all Israel: there was none that followed the house of David, but the tribe of Judah only.

units.leftText: And when Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he mobilized the whole house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin — 180,000 chosen warriors — to fight against the house of Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
units.rightText: And when Rehoboam was come to Jerusalem, he assembled all the house of Judah, and the tribe of Benjamin, a hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men, that were warriors, to fight against the house of Israel, to bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam the son of Solomon.

units.leftText: But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God:
units.rightText: But the word of God came unto Shemaiah the man of God, saying,

units.leftText: “Tell Rehoboam son of Solomon king of Judah, all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and the rest of the people
units.rightText: Speak unto Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and unto all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people, saying,

units.leftText: that this is what the LORD says: ‘You are not to go up and fight against your brothers, the Israelites. Each of you must return home, for this is My doing.’” So they listened to the word of the LORD and turned back according to the word of the LORD. Jeroboam’s Idolatry
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah, Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren the children of Israel: return every man to his house; for this thing is of me. So they hearkened unto the word of Jehovah, and returned and went their way, according to the word of Jehovah.
