units.leftText: Then Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. And from there he went out and built Penuel.
units.rightText: Then Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill-country of Ephraim, and dwelt therein; and he went out from thence, and built Penuel.
leftNotes: 12:25 Penuel is a variant of Peniel; see Genesis 32:30|GEN 32:30*.

units.leftText: Jeroboam said in his heart, “Now the kingdom might revert to the house of David.
units.rightText: And Jeroboam said in his heart, Now will the kingdom return to the house of David:

units.leftText: If these people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of the LORD at Jerusalem, their hearts will return to their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah; then they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.”
units.rightText: if this people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of Jehovah at Jerusalem, then will the heart of this people turn again unto their lord, even unto Rehoboam king of Judah; and they will kill me, and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.

units.leftText: After seeking advice, the king made two golden calves and said to the people, “Going up to Jerusalem is too much for you. Here, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.”
units.rightText: Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold; and he said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
leftNotes: 12:28 Hebrew to them

units.leftText: One calf he set up in Bethel, and the other in Dan.
units.rightText: And he set the one in Beth-el, and the other put he in Dan.

units.leftText: And this thing became a sin; the people walked as far as Dan to worship before one of the calves.
units.rightText: And this thing became a sin; for the people went to worship before the one, even unto Dan.
leftNotes: 12:30 Likely reading of the original Hebrew text; MT the people walked to the one as far as Dan; LXX the people went to the one at Bethel and to the other as far as Dan

units.leftText: Jeroboam also built shrines on the high places and appointed from every class of people priests who were not Levites.
units.rightText: And he made houses of high places, and made priests from among all the people, that were not of the sons of Levi.

units.leftText: And Jeroboam ordained a feast on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the feast that was in Judah, and he offered sacrifices on the altar; he made this offering in Bethel to sacrifice to the calves he had set up, and he installed priests in Bethel for the high places he had set up.
units.rightText: And Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that is in Judah, and he went up unto the altar; so did he in Beth-el, sacrificing unto the calves that he had made: and he placed in Beth-el the priests of the high places that he had made.
leftNotes: 12:32 This feast was exactly one month after the annual Feast of Tabernacles in Judah; see Leviticus 23:34|LEV 23:34*.

units.leftText: On the fifteenth day of the eighth month, a month of his own choosing, Jeroboam offered sacrifices on the altar he had set up in Bethel. So he ordained a feast for the Israelites, offered sacrifices on the altar, and burned incense.
units.rightText: And he went up unto the altar which he had made in Beth-el on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, even in the month which he had devised of his own heart: and he ordained a feast for the children of Israel, and went up unto the altar, to burn incense.

units.leftText: Suddenly, as Jeroboam was standing beside the altar to burn incense, there came a man of God from Judah to Bethel by the word of the LORD.
units.rightText: And, behold, there came a man of God out of Judah by the word of Jehovah unto Beth-el: and Jeroboam was standing by the altar to burn incense.

units.leftText: And he cried out against the altar by the word of the LORD, “O altar, O altar, this is what the LORD says: ‘A son named Josiah will be born to the house of David, and upon you he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense upon you, and human bones will be burned upon you.’”
units.rightText: And he cried against the altar by the word of Jehovah, and said, O altar, altar, thus saith Jehovah: Behold, a son shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name; and upon thee shall he sacrifice the priests of the high places that burn incense upon thee, and men’s bones shall they burn upon thee.

units.leftText: That day the man of God gave a sign, saying, “The LORD has spoken this sign: ‘Surely the altar will be split apart, and the ashes upon it will be poured out.’”
units.rightText: And he gave a sign the same day, saying, This is the sign which Jehovah hath spoken: Behold, the altar shall be rent, and the ashes that are upon it shall be poured out.

units.leftText: Now when King Jeroboam, who was at the altar in Bethel, heard the word that the man of God had cried out against it, he stretched out his hand and said, “Seize him!” But the hand he stretched out toward him withered, so that he could not pull it back.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the king heard the saying of the man of God, which he cried against the altar in Beth-el, that Jeroboam put forth his hand from the altar, saying, Lay hold on him. And his hand, which he put forth against him, dried up, so that he could not draw it back again to him.

units.leftText: And the altar was split apart, and the ashes poured out, according to the sign that the man of God had given by the word of the LORD.
units.rightText: The altar also was rent, and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God had given by the word of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then the king responded to the man of God, “Intercede with the LORD your God and pray for me that my hand may be restored.” So the man of God interceded with the LORD, and the king’s hand was restored to him as it was before.
units.rightText: And the king answered and said unto the man of God, Entreat now the favor of Jehovah thy God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored me again. And the man of God entreated Jehovah, and the king’s hand was restored him again, and became as it was before.

units.leftText: Then the king said to the man of God, “Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I will give you a reward.”
units.rightText: And the king said unto the man of God, Come home with me, and refresh thyself, and I will give thee a reward.

units.leftText: But the man of God replied, “If you were to give me half your possessions, I still would not go with you, nor would I eat bread or drink water in this place.
units.rightText: And the man of God said unto the king, If thou wilt give me half thy house, I will not go in with thee, neither will I eat bread nor drink water in this place;

units.leftText: For this is what I was commanded by the word of the LORD: ‘You must not eat bread or drink water or return by the way you came.’”
units.rightText: for so was it charged me by the word of Jehovah, saying, Thou shalt eat no bread, nor drink water, neither return by the way that thou camest.

units.leftText: So the man of God went another way and did not return by the way he had come to Bethel. The Old Prophet and the Man of God
units.rightText: So he went another way, and returned not by the way that he came to Beth-el.

units.leftText: Now a certain old prophet was living in Bethel, and his sons came and told him all the deeds that the man of God had done that day in Bethel. They also told their father the words that the man had spoken to the king.
units.rightText: Now there dwelt an old prophet in Beth-el; and one of his sons came and told him all the works that the man of God had done that day in Beth-el: the words which he had spoken unto the king, them also they told unto their father.
leftNotes: 13:11 LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate; Hebrew son

units.leftText: “Which way did he go?” their father asked.
units.rightText: And their father said unto them, What way went he? Now his sons had seen what way the man of God went, that came from Judah.

units.leftText: So the prophet said to his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.”
units.rightText: And he said unto his sons, Saddle me the ass. So they saddled him the ass; and he rode thereon.

units.leftText: and went after the man of God. He found him sitting under an oak tree and asked, “Are you the man of God who came from Judah?” “I am,” he replied.
units.rightText: And he went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak; and he said unto him, Art thou the man of God that camest from Judah? And he said, I am.
leftNotes: 13:14 Or a terebinth or a great tree

units.leftText: So the prophet said to the man of God, “Come home with me and eat some bread.”
units.rightText: Then he said unto him, Come home with me, and eat bread.

units.leftText: But the man replied, “I cannot go home with you, and I will not eat bread or drink water with you in this place.
units.rightText: And he said, I may not return with thee, nor go in with thee; neither will I eat bread nor drink water with thee in this place:

units.leftText: For I have been told by the word of the LORD: ‘You must not eat bread or drink water there or return by the way you came.’”
units.rightText: for it was said to me by the word of Jehovah, Thou shalt eat no bread nor drink water there, nor turn again to go by the way that thou camest.

units.leftText: Then the prophet replied, “I too am a prophet like you, and an angel spoke to me by the word of the LORD, saying, ‘Bring him back with you to your house, so that he may eat bread and drink water.’”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, I also am a prophet as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the word of Jehovah, saying, Bring him back with thee into thy house, that he may eat bread and drink water. But he lied unto him.

units.leftText: but the man of God went back with him, ate bread in his house, and drank water.
units.rightText: So he went back with him, and did eat bread in his house, and drank water.

units.leftText: While they were sitting at the table, the word of the LORD came to the prophet who had brought him back,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as they sat at the table, that the word of Jehovah came unto the prophet that brought him back;

units.leftText: and the prophet cried out to the man of God who had come from Judah, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Because you have defied the word of the LORD and have not kept the commandment that the LORD your God gave you,
units.rightText: and he cried unto the man of God that came from Judah, saying, Thus saith Jehovah, Forasmuch as thou hast been disobedient unto the mouth of Jehovah, and hast not kept the commandment which Jehovah thy God commanded thee,

units.leftText: but you went back and ate bread and drank water in the place where He told you not to do so, your body shall never reach the tomb of your fathers.’”
units.rightText: but camest back, and hast eaten bread and drunk water in the place of which he said to thee, Eat no bread, and drink no water; thy body shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers.

units.leftText: And after the man of God had finished eating and drinking, the old prophet who had brought him back saddled the donkey for him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, after he had eaten bread, and after he had drunk, that he saddled for him the ass, to wit, for the prophet whom he had brought back.

units.leftText: As he went on his way, a lion met him on the road and killed him, and his body was left lying in the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it.
units.rightText: And when he was gone, a lion met him by the way, and slew him: and his body was cast in the way, and the ass stood by it; the lion also stood by the body.

units.leftText: And there were men passing by who saw the body lying in the road with the lion standing beside it, and they went and reported this in the city where the old prophet lived.
units.rightText: And, behold, men passed by, and saw the body cast in the way, and the lion standing by the body; and they came and told it in the city where the old prophet dwelt.

units.leftText: When the prophet who had brought him back from his journey heard this, he said, “It is the man of God who disobeyed the command of the LORD. Therefore the LORD has delivered him to the lion, and it has mauled him and killed him, according to the word that the LORD had spoken to him.”
units.rightText: And when the prophet that brought him back from the way heard thereof, he said, It is the man of God, who was disobedient unto the mouth of Jehovah: therefore Jehovah hath delivered him unto the lion, which hath torn him, and slain him, according to the word of Jehovah, which he spake unto him.

units.leftText: Then the old prophet instructed his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.” So they saddled it,
units.rightText: And he spake to his sons, saying, Saddle me the ass. And they saddled it.

units.leftText: and he went and found the body lying in the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it. The lion had not eaten the body or mauled the donkey.
units.rightText: And he went and found his body cast in the way, and the ass and the lion standing by the body: the lion had not eaten the body, nor torn the ass.

units.leftText: So the old prophet lifted up the body of the man of God, laid it on the donkey, and brought it back to his own city to mourn for him and bury him.
units.rightText: And the prophet took up the body of the man of God, and laid it upon the ass, and brought it back; and he came to the city of the old prophet, to mourn, and to bury him.

units.leftText: Then he laid the body in his own tomb, and they lamented over him, “Oh, my brother!”
units.rightText: And he laid his body in his own grave; and they mourned over him, saying, Alas, my brother!

units.leftText: After he had buried him, the prophet said to his sons, “When I die, you must bury me in the tomb where the man of God is buried. Lay my bones beside his bones,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, after he had buried him, that he spake to his sons, saying, When I am dead, then bury me in the sepulchre wherein the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones.

units.leftText: for the message that he cried out by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel and against all the shrines on the high places in the cities of Samaria will surely come to pass.”
units.rightText: For the saying which he cried by the word of Jehovah against the altar in Beth-el, and against all the houses of the high places which are in the cities of Samaria, shall surely come to pass.

units.leftText: Even after these events, Jeroboam did not repent of his evil ways, but again he appointed priests for the high places from every class of people. He ordained anyone who desired to be a priest of the high places.
units.rightText: After this thing Jeroboam returned not from his evil way, but made again from among all the people priests of the high places: whosoever would, he consecrated him, that there might be priests of the high places.

units.leftText: And this was the sin of the house of Jeroboam that led to its extermination and destruction from the face of the earth.
units.rightText: And this thing became sin unto the house of Jeroboam, even to cut it off, and to destroy it from off the face of the earth.

units.leftText: At that time Abijah son of Jeroboam became ill,
units.rightText: At that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell sick.

units.leftText: and Jeroboam said to his wife, “Now get up, disguise yourself so they will not recognize you as my wife, and go to Shiloh. For Ahijah the prophet is there; it was he who spoke about my kingship over this people.
units.rightText: And Jeroboam said to his wife, Arise, I pray thee, and disguise thyself, that thou be not known to be the wife of Jeroboam; and get thee to Shiloh: behold, there is Ahijah the prophet, who spake concerning me that I should be king over this people.

units.leftText: Take with you ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what will become of the boy.”
units.rightText: And take with thee ten loaves, and cakes, and a cruse of honey, and go to him: he will tell thee what shall become of the child.

units.leftText: Jeroboam’s wife did as instructed; she arose and went to Shiloh and arrived at Ahijah’s house. Now Ahijah could not see, for his eyes were dim because of his age.
units.rightText: And Jeroboam’s wife did so, and arose, and went to Shiloh, and came to the house of Ahijah. Now Ahijah could not see; for his eyes were set by reason of his age.

units.leftText: But the LORD had said to Ahijah, “Behold, the wife of Jeroboam is coming to ask you about her son, for he is ill. You are to say such and such to her, because when she arrives, she will be disguised.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Ahijah, Behold, the wife of Jeroboam cometh to inquire of thee concerning her son; for he is sick: thus and thus shalt thou say unto her; for it will be, when she cometh in, that she will feign herself to be another woman.

units.leftText: So when Ahijah heard the sound of her feet entering the door, he said, “Come in, wife of Jeroboam! Why are you disguised? For I have been sent to you with bad news.
units.rightText: And it was so, when Ahijah heard the sound of her feet, as she came in at the door, that he said, Come in, thou wife of Jeroboam; why feignest thou thyself to be another? for I am sent to thee with heavy tidings.

units.leftText: Go, tell Jeroboam that this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I raised you up from among the people and appointed you ruler over My people Israel.
units.rightText: Go, tell Jeroboam, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel: Forasmuch as I exalted thee from among the people, and made thee prince over my people Israel,

units.leftText: I tore the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it to you. But you have not been like My servant David, who kept My commandments and followed Me with all his heart, doing only what was right in My eyes.
units.rightText: and rent the kingdom away from the house of David, and gave it thee; and yet thou hast not been as my servant David, who kept my commandments, and who followed me with all his heart, to do that only which was right in mine eyes,

units.leftText: You have done more evil than all who came before you. You have proceeded to make for yourself other gods and molten images to provoke Me, and you have flung Me behind your back.
units.rightText: but hast done evil above all that were before thee, and hast gone and made thee other gods, and molten images, to provoke me to anger, and hast cast me behind thy back:

units.leftText: Because of all this, behold, I am bringing disaster on the house of Jeroboam: I will cut off from Jeroboam every male, both slave and free, in Israel; I will burn up the house of Jeroboam as one burns up dung until it is gone!
units.rightText: therefore, behold, I will bring evil upon the house of Jeroboam, and will cut off from Jeroboam every man-child, him that is shut up and him that is left at large in Israel, and will utterly sweep away the house of Jeroboam, as a man sweepeth away dung, till it be all gone.
leftNotes: 14:10 Literally (all) those who urinate against a wall

units.leftText: Anyone belonging to Jeroboam who dies in the city will be eaten by dogs, and anyone who dies in the field will be eaten by the birds of the air.’ For the LORD has spoken.
units.rightText: Him that dieth of Jeroboam in the city shall the dogs eat; and him that dieth in the field shall the birds of the heavens eat: for Jehovah hath spoken it.

units.leftText: As for you, get up and go home. When your feet enter the city, the child will die.
units.rightText: Arise thou therefore, get thee to thy house: and when thy feet enter into the city, the child shall die.

units.leftText: All Israel will mourn for him and bury him. For this is the only one belonging to Jeroboam who will receive a proper burial, because only in him has the LORD, the God of Israel, found any good in the house of Jeroboam.
units.rightText: And all Israel shall mourn for him, and bury him; for he only of Jeroboam shall come to the grave, because in him there is found some good thing toward Jehovah, the God of Israel, in the house of Jeroboam.
leftNotes: 14:13 Literally who will come to the grave

units.leftText: Moreover , the LORD will raise up for Himself a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jeroboam. This is the day — yes, even today!
units.rightText: Moreover Jehovah will raise him up a king over Israel, who shall cut off the house of Jeroboam that day: but what? even now.

units.leftText: For the LORD will strike Israel as a reed is shaken in the water. He will uproot Israel from this good land that He gave their fathers, and He will scatter them beyond the Euphrates, because they have made their Asherah poles, provoking the LORD to anger.
units.rightText: For Jehovah will smite Israel, as a reed is shaken in the water; and he will root up Israel out of this good land which he gave to their fathers, and will scatter them beyond the River, because they have made their Asherim, provoking Jehovah to anger.
leftNotes: 14:15 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: So He will give Israel over on account of the sins Jeroboam has committed and has caused Israel to commit.”
units.rightText: And he will give Israel up because of the sins of Jeroboam, which he hath sinned, and wherewith he hath made Israel to sin.

units.leftText: Then Jeroboam’s wife got up and departed for Tirzah, and as soon as she stepped over the threshold of the house, the boy died.
units.rightText: And Jeroboam’s wife arose, and departed, and came to Tirzah: and as she came to the threshold of the house, the child died.

units.leftText: And they buried him, and all Israel mourned for him, according to the word that the LORD had spoken through His servant Ahijah the prophet. Nadab Succeeds Jeroboam
units.rightText: And all Israel buried him, and mourned for him, according to the word of Jehovah, which he spake by his servant Ahijah the prophet.

units.leftText: As for the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he waged war and how he reigned, they are indeed written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
units.rightText: And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he warred, and how he reigned, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

units.leftText: And the length of Jeroboam’s reign was twenty-two years, and he rested with his fathers, and his son Nadab reigned in his place. Rehoboam Reigns in Judah (2 Chronicles 12:13–14|2CH 12:13-14*)
units.rightText: And the days which Jeroboam reigned were two and twenty years: and he slept with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned in Judah. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen from all the tribes of Israel in which to put His Name. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonite.
units.rightText: And Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty and one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which Jehovah had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there: and his mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonitess.

units.leftText: And Judah did evil in the sight of the LORD, and by the sins they committed they provoked Him to jealous anger more than all their fathers had done.
units.rightText: And Judah did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah, and they provoked him to jealousy with their sins which they committed, above all that their fathers had done.

units.leftText: They also built for themselves high places, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.
units.rightText: For they also built them high places, and pillars, and Asherim, on every high hill, and under every green tree;

units.leftText: There were even male shrine prostitutes in the land. They imitated all the abominations of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites. Shishak Raids Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 12:1–12|2CH 12:1-12*)
units.rightText: and there were also sodomites in the land: they did according to all the abominations of the nations which Jehovah drove out before the children of Israel.

units.leftText: In the fifth year of Rehoboam’s reign, Shishak king of Egypt attacked Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the fifth year of king Rehoboam, that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem;

units.leftText: He seized the treasures of the house of the LORD and of the royal palace. He took everything, including all the gold shields that Solomon had made.
units.rightText: and he took away the treasures of the house of Jehovah, and the treasures of the king’s house; he even took away all: and he took away all the shields of gold which Solomon had made.

units.leftText: Then King Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place and committed them to the care of the captains of the guard on duty at the entrance to the royal palace.
units.rightText: And king Rehoboam made in their stead shields of brass, and committed them to the hands of the captains of the guard, who kept the door of the king’s house.

units.leftText: And whenever the king entered the house of the LORD, the guards would bear the shields, and later they would return them to the guardroom.
units.rightText: And it was so, that, as oft as the king went into the house of Jehovah, the guard bare them, and brought them back into the guard-chamber.

units.leftText: As for the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, along with all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
units.rightText: Now the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

units.leftText: There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam throughout their days.
units.rightText: And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.

units.leftText: And Rehoboam rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David; his mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonite. And his son Abijam reigned in his place.
units.rightText: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David: and his mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonitess. And Abijam his son reigned in his stead.
leftNotes: 14:31 Abijam is a variant of Abijah; some Hebrew manuscripts and LXX Abijah; see 2 Chronicles 12:16|2CH 12:16*.

units.leftText: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam became king of Judah,
units.rightText: Now in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam the son of Nebat began Abijam to reign over Judah.
leftNotes: 15:1 Abijam is a variant of Abijah; some Hebrew manuscripts and LXX Abijah; also in verses 3, 6, 7, and 8; see 2 Chronicles 12:16|2CH 12:16*.

units.leftText: and he reigned in Jerusalem three years. His mother’s name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
units.rightText: Three years reigned he in Jerusalem: and his mother’s name was Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
leftNotes: 15:2 Abishalom is a variant of Absalom; also in verse 10; see 2 Chronicles 11:20|2CH 11:20*.

units.leftText: And Abijam walked in all the sins that his father before him had committed, and his heart was not as fully devoted to the LORD his God as the heart of David his forefather had been.
units.rightText: And he walked in all the sins of his father, which he had done before him; and his heart was not perfect with Jehovah his God, as the heart of David his father.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, for the sake of David, the LORD his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem by raising up a son to succeed him and to make Jerusalem strong.
units.rightText: Nevertheless for David’s sake did Jehovah his God give him a lamp in Jerusalem, to set up his son after him, and to establish Jerusalem;

units.leftText: For David had done what was right in the eyes of the LORD and had not turned aside from anything the LORD commanded all the days of his life, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
units.rightText: because David did that which was right in the eyes of Jehovah, and turned not aside from anything that he commanded him all the days of his life, save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.

units.leftText: And there was war between the houses of Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of Abijam’s life.
units.rightText: Now there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.
leftNotes: 15:6 Literally war between Rehoboam (most Hebrew manuscripts); some Hebrew manuscripts and Syriac war between Abijam (that is, Abijah); most LXX texts do not contain this verse.
15:6 Literally of his life

units.leftText: As for the rest of the acts of Abijam, along with all his accomplishments, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah? And there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
units.rightText: And the rest of the acts of Abijam, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? And there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.

units.leftText: And Abijam rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David, and his son Asa reigned in his place. Asa Reigns in Judah (2 Chronicles 14:1–15|2CH 14:1-15*; 2 Chronicles 15:8–19|2CH 15:8-19*)
units.rightText: And Abijam slept with his fathers; and they buried him in the city of David: and Asa his son reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: In the twentieth year of Jeroboam’s reign over Israel, Asa became king of Judah,
units.rightText: And in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel began Asa to reign over Judah.

units.leftText: and he reigned in Jerusalem forty-one years. His grandmother’s name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
units.rightText: And forty and one years reigned he in Jerusalem: and his mother’s name was Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
leftNotes: 15:10 Or The queen mother’s; Hebrew His mother’s; see verses 2 and 13.

units.leftText: And Asa did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his father David had done.
units.rightText: And Asa did that which was right in the eyes of Jehovah, as did David his father.

units.leftText: He banished the male shrine prostitutes from the land and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.
units.rightText: And he put away the sodomites out of the land, and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.

units.leftText: He also removed his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother because she had made a detestable Asherah pole. Asa chopped down the pole and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
units.rightText: And also Maacah his mother he removed from being queen, because she had made an abominable image for an Asherah; and Asa cut down her image, and burnt it at the brook Kidron.

units.leftText: The high places were not removed, but Asa’s heart was fully devoted to the LORD all his days.
units.rightText: But the high places were not taken away: nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect with Jehovah all his days.

units.leftText: And he brought into the house of the LORD the silver and gold and the articles that he and his father had dedicated. War between Asa and Baasha (2 Chronicles 16:1–6|2CH 16:1-6*)
units.rightText: And he brought into the house of Jehovah the things that his father had dedicated, and the things that himself had dedicated, silver, and gold, and vessels.

units.leftText: Now there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel throughout their days.
units.rightText: And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.

units.leftText: Baasha king of Israel went to war against Judah and fortified Ramah to prevent anyone from leaving or entering the territory of Asa king of Judah.
units.rightText: And Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah, and built Ramah, that he might not suffer any one to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.

units.leftText: So Asa withdrew all the silver and gold that remained in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the royal palace. He entrusted it to his servants and sent them with this message to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon, the son of Hezion, the king of Aram, who was ruling in Damascus:
units.rightText: Then Asa took all the silver and the gold that were left in the treasures of the house of Jehovah, and the treasures of the king’s house, and delivered them into the hand of his servants; and king Asa sent them to Ben-hadad, the son of Tabrimmon, the son of Hezion, king of Syria, that dwelt at Damascus, saying,

units.leftText: “Let there be a treaty between me and you as there was between my father and your father. See, I have sent you a gift of silver and gold. Now go and break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me.”
units.rightText: There is a league between me and thee, between my father and thy father: behold, I have sent unto thee a present of silver and gold; go, break thy league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.
leftNotes: 15:19 Forms of the Hebrew berit are translated in most passages as covenant; twice in this verse.

units.leftText: And Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel, conquering Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah, and the whole land of Naphtali, including the region of Chinnereth.
units.rightText: And Ben-hadad hearkened unto king Asa, and sent the captains of his armies against the cities of Israel, and smote Ijon, and Dan, and Abel-beth-maacah, and all Chinneroth, with all the land of Naphtali.

units.leftText: When Baasha learned of this, he stopped fortifying Ramah and withdrew to Tirzah.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Baasha heard thereof, that he left off building Ramah, and dwelt in Tirzah.

units.leftText: Then King Asa summoned all the men of Judah, with no exceptions, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and the timbers Baasha had used for building. And with these materials King Asa built up Geba of Benjamin, as well as Mizpah. Jehoshaphat Succeeds Asa (2 Chronicles 17:1–19|2CH 17:1-19*)
units.rightText: Then king Asa made a proclamation unto all Judah; none was exempted: and they carried away the stones of Ramah, and the timber thereof, wherewith Baasha had builded; and king Asa built therewith Geba of Benjamin, and Mizpah.
leftNotes: 15:22 Or Then King Asa made a proclamation throughout all Judah

units.leftText: Now the rest of the acts of Asa, along with all his might, all his accomplishments, and the cities he built, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah? In his old age, however, he became diseased in his feet.
units.rightText: Now the rest of all the acts of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the cities which he built, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? But in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.

units.leftText: And Asa rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the city of his father David, and his son Jehoshaphat reigned in his place. Nadab Reigns in Israel
units.rightText: And Asa slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father; and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: In the second year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel, and he reigned two years.
units.rightText: And Nadab the son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah; and he reigned over Israel two years.

units.leftText: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD and walked in the way of his father and in his sin, which he had caused Israel to commit.
units.rightText: And he did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah, and walked in the way of his father, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin.

units.leftText: Then Baasha son of Ahijah of the house of Issachar conspired against Nadab, and Baasha struck him down at Gibbethon of the Philistines while Nadab and all Israel were besieging the city.
units.rightText: And Baasha the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him; and Baasha smote him at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines; for Nadab and all Israel were laying siege to Gibbethon.

units.leftText: In the third year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Baasha killed Nadab and reigned in his place.
units.rightText: Even in the third year of Asa king of Judah did Baasha slay him, and reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: As soon as Baasha became king, he struck down the entire household of Jeroboam. He did not leave to Jeroboam anyone who breathed, but destroyed them all according to the word that the LORD had spoken through His servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
units.rightText: And it came to pass that, as soon as he was king, he smote all the house of Jeroboam: he left not to Jeroboam any that breathed, until he had destroyed him; according unto the saying of Jehovah, which he spake by his servant Ahijah the Shilonite;

units.leftText: because of the sins Jeroboam had committed and had caused Israel to commit, and because he had provoked the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger.
units.rightText: for the sins of Jeroboam which he sinned, and wherewith he made Israel to sin, because of his provocation wherewith he provoked Jehovah, the God of Israel, to anger.

units.leftText: As for the rest of the acts of Nadab, along with all his accomplishments, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
units.rightText: Now the rest of the acts of Nadab, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

units.leftText: And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel throughout their days. Baasha Reigns in Israel
units.rightText: And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.

units.leftText: In the third year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king of all Israel, and he reigned in Tirzah twenty-four years.
units.rightText: In the third year of Asa king of Judah began Baasha the son of Ahijah to reign over all Israel in Tirzah, and reigned twenty and four years.

units.leftText: And Baasha did evil in the sight of the LORD and walked in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin, which he had caused Israel to commit.
units.rightText: And he did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah, and walked in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin.

units.leftText: Then the word of the LORD came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, saying:
units.rightText: And the word of Jehovah came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,

units.leftText: “Even though I lifted you out of the dust and made you ruler over My people Israel, you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and have caused My people Israel to sin and to provoke Me to anger by their sins.
units.rightText: Forasmuch as I exalted thee out of the dust, and made thee prince over my people Israel, and thou hast walked in the way of Jeroboam, and hast made my people Israel to sin, to provoke me to anger with their sins;

units.leftText: So now I will consume Baasha and his house, and I will make your house like that of Jeroboam son of Nebat:
units.rightText: behold, I will utterly sweep away Baasha and his house; and I will make thy house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

units.leftText: Anyone belonging to Baasha who dies in the city will be eaten by dogs, and anyone who dies in the field will be eaten by the birds of the air.”
units.rightText: Him that dieth of Baasha in the city shall the dogs eat; and him that dieth of his in the field shall the birds of the heavens eat.

units.leftText: As for the rest of the acts of Baasha, along with his accomplishments and might, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
units.rightText: Now the rest of the acts of Baasha, and what he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

units.leftText: And Baasha rested with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah reigned in his place.
units.rightText: And Baasha slept with his fathers, and was buried in Tirzah; and Elah his son reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: Moreover, the word of the LORD came through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha and his house, because of all the evil he had done in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger with the work of his hands and becoming like the house of Jeroboam, and also because Baasha had struck down the house of Jeroboam. Elah Reigns in Israel
units.rightText: And moreover by the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani came the word of Jehovah against Baasha, and against his house, both because of all the evil that he did in the sight of Jehovah, to provoke him to anger with the work of his hands, in being like the house of Jeroboam, and because he smote him.

units.leftText: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel, and he reigned in Tirzah two years.
units.rightText: In the twenty and sixth year of Asa king of Judah began Elah the son of Baasha to reign over Israel in Tirzah, and reigned two years.

units.leftText: However, while Elah was in Tirzah getting drunk in the house of Arza the steward of his household there, Elah’s servant Zimri, the commander of half his chariots, conspired against him.
units.rightText: And his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspired against him. Now he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, who was over the household in Tirzah:

units.leftText: So in the twenty-seventh year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Zimri went in, struck Elah down, and killed him. And Zimri reigned in his place.
units.rightText: and Zimri went in and smote him, and killed him, in the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: As soon as Zimri began to reign and was seated on the throne, he struck down the entire household of Baasha. He did not leave a single male, whether a kinsman or friend.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, that he smote all the house of Baasha: he left him not a single man-child, neither of his kinsfolks, nor of his friends.

units.leftText: So Zimri destroyed the entire household of Baasha, according to the word that the LORD had spoken against Baasha through Jehu the prophet.
units.rightText: Thus did Zimri destroy all the house of Baasha, according to the word of Jehovah, which he spake against Baasha by Jehu the prophet,

units.leftText: This happened because of all the sins Baasha and his son Elah had committed and had caused Israel to commit, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.
units.rightText: for all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, which they sinned, and wherewith they made Israel to sin, to provoke Jehovah, the God of Israel, to anger with their vanities.

units.leftText: As for the rest of the acts of Elah, along with all his accomplishments, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel? Zimri Reigns in Israel
units.rightText: Now the rest of the acts of Elah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

units.leftText: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Zimri reigned in Tirzah for seven days. Now the troops were encamped against Gibbethon of the Philistines,
units.rightText: In the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah did Zimri reign seven days in Tirzah. Now the people were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.

units.leftText: and the people in the camp heard that Zimri had conspired against the king and struck him down. So there in the camp that very day, all Israel proclaimed Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel.
units.rightText: And the people that were encamped heard say, Zimri hath conspired, and hath also smitten the king: wherefore all Israel made Omri, the captain of the host, king over Israel that day in the camp.

units.leftText: Then Omri and all the Israelites marched up from Gibbethon and besieged Tirzah.
units.rightText: And Omri went up from Gibbethon, and all Israel with him, and they besieged Tirzah.

units.leftText: When Zimri saw that the city was captured, he entered the citadel of the royal palace and burned it down upon himself. So he died
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Zimri saw that the city was taken, that he went into the castle of the king’s house, and burnt the king’s house over him with fire, and died,

units.leftText: because of the sins he had committed, doing evil in the sight of the LORD and following the example of Jeroboam and the sin he had committed and had caused Israel to commit.
units.rightText: for his sins which he sinned in doing that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah, in walking in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin which he did, to make Israel to sin.

units.leftText: As for the rest of the acts of Zimri and the treason he committed, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel? Omri Reigns in Israel
units.rightText: Now the rest of the acts of Zimri, and his treason that he wrought, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

units.leftText: At that time the people of Israel were divided: Half of the people supported Tibni son of Ginath as king, and half supported Omri.
units.rightText: Then were the people of Israel divided into two parts: half of the people followed Tibni the son of Ginath, to make him king; and half followed Omri.

units.leftText: But the followers of Omri proved stronger than those of Tibni son of Ginath. So Tibni died and Omri became king.
units.rightText: But the people that followed Omri prevailed against the people that followed Tibni the son of Ginath: so Tibni died, and Omri reigned.

units.leftText: In the thirty-first year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Omri became king of Israel, and he reigned twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.
units.rightText: In the thirty and first year of Asa king of Judah began Omri to reign over Israel, and reigned twelve years: six years reigned he in Tirzah.

units.leftText: He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver and built a city there, calling it Samaria after the name of Shemer, who had owned the hill.
units.rightText: And he bought the hill Samaria of Shemer for two talents of silver; and he built on the hill, and called the name of the city which he built, after the name of Shemer, the owner of the hill, Samaria.
leftNotes: 16:24 2 talents is approximately 151 pounds or 68.4 kilograms of silver.

units.leftText: But Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD and acted more wickedly than all who were before him.
units.rightText: And Omri did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah, and dealt wickedly above all that were before him.

units.leftText: For he walked in all the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins, which he caused Israel to commit, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.
units.rightText: For he walked in all the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and in his sins wherewith he made Israel to sin, to provoke Jehovah, the God of Israel, to anger with their vanities.

units.leftText: As for the rest of the acts of Omri, along with his accomplishments and the might he exercised, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
units.rightText: Now the rest of the acts of Omri which he did, and his might that he showed, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

units.leftText: And Omri rested with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab reigned in his place. Ahab Reigns in Israel, Marries Jezebel
units.rightText: So Omri slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria; and Ahab his son reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: In the thirty-eighth year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria twenty-two years.
units.rightText: And in the thirty and eighth year of Asa king of Judah began Ahab the son of Omri to reign over Israel: and Ahab the son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty and two years.

units.leftText: However, Ahab son of Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD, more than all who were before him.
units.rightText: And Ahab the son of Omri did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah above all that were before him.

units.leftText: And as if it were not enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, he even married Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and he then proceeded to serve and worship Baal.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as if it had been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, that he took to wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and went and served Baal, and worshipped him.

units.leftText: First, Ahab set up an altar for Baal in the temple of Baal that he had built in Samaria.
units.rightText: And he reared up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal, which he had built in Samaria.

units.leftText: Then he set up an Asherah pole. Thus Ahab did more to provoke the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel before him.
units.rightText: And Ahab made the Asherah; and Ahab did yet more to provoke Jehovah, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel that were before him.

units.leftText: In Ahab’s days, Hiel the Bethelite rebuilt Jericho. At the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and at the cost of Segub his youngest he set up its gates, according to the word that the LORD had spoken through Joshua son of Nun.
units.rightText: In his days did Hiel the Beth-elite build Jericho: he laid the foundation thereof with the loss of Abiram his first-born, and set up the gates thereof with the loss of his youngest son Segub, according to the word of Jehovah, which he spake by Joshua the son of Nun.
leftNotes: 16:34 See Joshua 6:26|JOS 6:26*.

units.leftText: Now Elijah the Tishbite, who was among the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, “As surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there will be neither dew nor rain in these years except at my word!”
units.rightText: And Elijah the Tishbite, who was of the sojourners of Gilead, said unto Ahab, As Jehovah, the God of Israel, liveth, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word.
leftNotes: 17:1 Or who was from Tishbe in Gilead

units.leftText: Then a revelation from the LORD came to Elijah:
units.rightText: And the word of Jehovah came unto him, saying,

units.leftText: “Leave here, turn eastward, and hide yourself by the Brook of Cherith, east of the Jordan.
units.rightText: Get thee hence, and turn thee eastward, and hide thyself by the brook Cherith, that is before the Jordan.
leftNotes: 17:3 Or the Cherith Ravine, near the Jordan; also in verse 5

units.leftText: And you are to drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.”
units.rightText: And it shall be, that thou shalt drink of the brook; and I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there.

units.leftText: So Elijah did what the LORD had told him, and he went and lived by the Brook of Cherith, east of the Jordan.
units.rightText: So he went and did according unto the word of Jehovah; for he went and dwelt by the brook Cherith, that is before the Jordan.

units.leftText: The ravens would bring him bread and meat in the morning and evening, and he would drink from the brook.
units.rightText: And the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the brook.

units.leftText: Some time later, however, the brook dried up because there had been no rain in the land. The Widow of Zarephath
units.rightText: And it came to pass after a while, that the brook dried up, because there was no rain in the land.

units.leftText: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah:
units.rightText: And the word of Jehovah came unto him, saying,

units.leftText: “Get up and go to Zarephath of Sidon, and stay there. Behold, I have commanded a widow there to provide for you.”
units.rightText: Arise, get thee to Zarephath, which belongeth to Sidon, and dwell there: behold, I have commanded a widow there to sustain thee.

units.leftText: So Elijah got up and went to Zarephath. When he arrived at the city gate, there was a widow gathering sticks. Elijah called to her and said, “Please bring me a little water in a cup, so that I may drink.”
units.rightText: So he arose and went to Zarephath; and when he came to the gate of the city, behold, a widow was there gathering sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.

units.leftText: And as she was going to get it, he called to her and said, “Please bring me a piece of bread.”
units.rightText: And as she was going to fetch it, he called to her, and said, Bring me, I pray thee, a morsel of bread in thy hand.

units.leftText: But she replied, “As surely as the LORD your God lives, I have no bread— only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. Look, I am gathering a couple of sticks to take home and prepare a meal for myself and my son, so that we may eat it and die.”
units.rightText: And she said, As Jehovah thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but a handful of meal in the jar, and a little oil in the cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.

units.leftText: “Do not be afraid,” Elijah said to her. “Go and do as you have said. But first make me a small cake of bread from what you have, and bring it out to me. Afterward, make some for yourself and your son,
units.rightText: And Elijah said unto her, Fear not; go and do as thou hast said; but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it forth unto me, and afterward make for thee and for thy son.

units.leftText: for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘The jar of flour will not be exhausted and the jug of oil will not run dry until the day the LORD sends rain upon the face of the earth.’”
units.rightText: For thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, The jar of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that Jehovah sendeth rain upon the earth.

units.leftText: So she went and did according to the word of Elijah, and there was food every day for Elijah and the woman and her household.
units.rightText: And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days.

units.leftText: The jar of flour was not exhausted and the jug of oil did not run dry, according to the word that the LORD had spoken through Elijah. Elijah Raises the Widow’s Son
units.rightText: The jar of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of Jehovah, which he spake by Elijah.

units.leftText: Later, the son of the woman who owned the house became ill, and his sickness grew worse and worse, until no breath remained in him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass after these things, that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick; and his sickness was so sore, that there was no breath left in him.

units.leftText: “O man of God,” said the woman to Elijah, “what have you done to me? Have you come to remind me of my iniquity and cause the death of my son?”
units.rightText: And she said unto Elijah, What have I to do with thee, O thou man of God? thou art come unto me to bring my sin to remembrance, and to slay my son!

units.leftText: But Elijah said to her, “Give me your son.”
units.rightText: And he said unto her, Give me thy son. And he took him out of her bosom, and carried him up into the chamber, where he abode, and laid him upon his own bed.

units.leftText: Then he cried out to the LORD, “O LORD my God, have You also brought tragedy on this widow who has opened her home to me, by causing her son to die?”
units.rightText: And he cried unto Jehovah, and said, O Jehovah my God, hast thou also brought evil upon the widow with whom I sojourn, by slaying her son?

units.leftText: Then he stretched himself out over the child three times and cried out to the LORD, “O LORD my God, please let this boy’s life return to him!”
units.rightText: And he stretched himself upon the child three times, and cried unto Jehovah, and said, O Jehovah my God, I pray thee, let this child’s soul come into him again.

units.leftText: And the LORD listened to the voice of Elijah, and the child’s life returned to him, and he lived.
units.rightText: And Jehovah hearkened unto the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.

units.leftText: Then Elijah took the child, brought him down from the upper room into the house, and gave him to his mother. “Look, your son is alive,” Elijah declared.
units.rightText: And Elijah took the child, and brought him down out of the chamber into the house, and delivered him unto his mother; and Elijah said, See, thy son liveth.

units.leftText: Then the woman said to Elijah, “Now I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the LORD from your mouth is truth.”
units.rightText: And the woman said to Elijah, Now I know that thou art a man of God, and that the word of Jehovah in thy mouth is truth.

units.leftText: After a long time, in the third year of the drought, the word of the LORD came to Elijah: “Go and present yourself to Ahab, and I will send rain upon the face of the earth.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass after many days, that the word of Jehovah came to Elijah, in the third year, saying, Go, show thyself unto Ahab; and I will send rain upon the earth.
leftNotes: 18:1 Literally And the days were many, and in the third year,

units.leftText: So Elijah went to present himself to Ahab. The famine was severe in Samaria,
units.rightText: And Elijah went to show himself unto Ahab. And the famine was sore in Samaria.

units.leftText: and Ahab summoned Obadiah, who was in charge of the palace.
units.rightText: And Ahab called Obadiah, who was over the household. (Now Obadiah feared Jehovah greatly:

units.leftText: for when Jezebel had slaughtered the prophets of the LORD, Obadiah had taken a hundred prophets and hidden them, fifty men per cave, providing them with food and water.)
units.rightText: for it was so, when Jezebel cut off the prophets of Jehovah, that Obadiah took a hundred prophets, and hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water.)

units.leftText: Then Ahab said to Obadiah, “Go throughout the land to every spring and every valley. Perhaps we will find grass to keep the horses and mules alive so that we will not have to destroy any livestock.”
units.rightText: And Ahab said unto Obadiah, Go through the land, unto all the fountains of water, and unto all the brooks: peradventure we may find grass and save the horses and mules alive, that we lose not all the beasts.

units.leftText: So they divided the land to explore. Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went the other way by himself.
units.rightText: So they divided the land between them to pass throughout it: Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went another way by himself.

units.leftText: Now as Obadiah went on his way, Elijah suddenly met him. When Obadiah recognized him, he fell facedown and said, “Is it you, my lord Elijah?”
units.rightText: And as Obadiah was in the way, behold, Elijah met him: and he knew him, and fell on his face, and said, Is it thou, my lord Elijah?

units.leftText: “It is I,” he answered. “Go tell your master, ‘Elijah is here!’”
units.rightText: And he answered him, It is I: go, tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah is here.

units.leftText: But Obadiah replied, “How have I sinned, that you are handing your servant over to Ahab to put me to death?
units.rightText: And he said, Wherein have I sinned, that thou wouldest deliver thy servant into the hand of Ahab, to slay me?

units.leftText: As surely as the LORD your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent someone to search for you. When they said, ‘He is not here,’ he made that kingdom or nation swear that they had not found you.
units.rightText: As Jehovah thy God liveth, there is no nation or kingdom, whither my lord hath not sent to seek thee: and when they said, He is not here, he took an oath of the kingdom and nation, that they found thee not.

units.leftText: And now you say, ‘Go tell your master that Elijah is here!’
units.rightText: And now thou sayest, Go, tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah is here.

units.leftText: I do not know where the Spirit of the LORD may carry you off when I leave you. Then when I go and tell Ahab and he does not find you, he will kill me. But I, your servant, have feared the LORD from my youth.
units.rightText: And it will come to pass, as soon as I am gone from thee, that the Spirit of Jehovah will carry thee whither I know not; and so when I come and tell Ahab, and he cannot find thee, he will slay me: but I thy servant fear Jehovah from my youth.

units.leftText: Was it not reported to my lord what I did when Jezebel slaughtered the prophets of the LORD? I hid a hundred prophets of the LORD, fifty men per cave, and I provided them with food and water.
units.rightText: Was it not told my lord what I did when Jezebel slew the prophets of Jehovah, how I hid a hundred men of Jehovah’s prophets by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water?

units.leftText: And now you say, ‘Go tell your lord that Elijah is here!’ He will kill me!”
units.rightText: And now thou sayest, Go, tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah is here; and he will slay me.

units.leftText: Then Elijah said, “As surely as the LORD of Hosts lives, before whom I stand, I will present myself to Ahab today.” Elijah on Mount Carmel
units.rightText: And Elijah said, As Jehovah of hosts liveth, before whom I stand, I will surely show myself unto him to-day.

units.leftText: So Obadiah went to inform Ahab, who went to meet Elijah.
units.rightText: So Obadiah went to meet Ahab, and told him; and Ahab went to meet Elijah.

units.leftText: When Ahab saw Elijah, he said to him, “Is that you, O troubler of Israel?”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said unto him, Is it thou, thou troubler of Israel?

units.leftText: “I have not troubled Israel,” Elijah replied, “but you and your father’s house have, for you have forsaken the commandments of the LORD and have followed the Baals.
units.rightText: And he answered, I have not troubled Israel; but thou, and thy father’s house, in that ye have forsaken the commandments of Jehovah, and thou hast followed the Baalim.

units.leftText: Now summon all Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel, along with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah who eat at Jezebel’s table.”
units.rightText: Now therefore send, and gather to me all Israel unto mount Carmel, and the prophets of Baal four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the Asherah four hundred, that eat at Jezebel’s table.

units.leftText: So Ahab summoned all the Israelites and assembled the prophets on Mount Carmel.
units.rightText: So Ahab sent unto all the children of Israel, and gathered the prophets together unto mount Carmel.

units.leftText: Then Elijah approached all the people and said, “How long will you waver between two opinions? If the LORD is God, follow Him. But if Baal is God, follow him.” But the people did not answer a word.
units.rightText: And Elijah came near unto all the people, and said, How long go ye limping between the two sides? if Jehovah be God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.

units.leftText: Then Elijah said to the people, “I am the only remaining prophet of the LORD, but Baal has four hundred and fifty prophets.
units.rightText: Then said Elijah unto the people, I, even I only, am left a prophet of Jehovah; but Baal’s prophets are four hundred and fifty men.

units.leftText: Get two bulls for us. Let the prophets of Baal choose one bull for themselves, cut it into pieces, and place it on the wood but not light the fire. And I will prepare the other bull and place it on the wood but not light the fire.
units.rightText: Let them therefore give us two bullocks; and let them choose one bullock for themselves, and cut it in pieces, and lay it on the wood, and put no fire under; and I will dress the other bullock, and lay it on the wood, and put no fire under.

units.leftText: Then you may call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of the LORD. The God who answers by fire, He is God.” And all the people answered, “What you say is good.”
units.rightText: And call ye on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of Jehovah; and the God that answereth by fire, let him be God. And all the people answered and said, It is well spoken.

units.leftText: Then Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, “Since you are so numerous, choose for yourselves one bull and prepare it first. Then call on the name of your god, but do not light the fire.”
units.rightText: And Elijah said unto the prophets of Baal, Choose you one bullock for yourselves, and dress it first; for ye are many; and call on the name of your god, but put no fire under.

units.leftText: And they took the bull that was given them, prepared it, and called on the name of Baal from morning until noon, shouting, “O Baal, answer us!” But there was no sound, and no one answered as they leaped around the altar they had made.
units.rightText: And they took the bullock which was given them, and they dressed it, and called on the name of Baal from morning even until noon, saying, O Baal, hear us. But there was no voice, nor any that answered. And they leaped about the altar which was made.

units.leftText: At noon Elijah began to taunt them, saying, “Shout louder, for he is a god! Perhaps he is deep in thought, or occupied, or on a journey. Perhaps he is sleeping and must be awakened!”
units.rightText: And it came to pass at noon, that Elijah mocked them, and said, Cry aloud; for he is a god: either he is musing, or he is gone aside, or he is on a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth and must be awaked.

units.leftText: So they shouted louder and cut themselves with knives and lances, as was their custom, until the blood gushed over them.
units.rightText: And they cried aloud, and cut themselves after their manner with knives and lances, till the blood gushed out upon them.

units.leftText: Midday passed, and they kept on raving until the time of the evening sacrifice. But there was no response; no one answered, no one paid attention.
units.rightText: And it was so, when midday was past, that they prophesied until the time of the offering of the evening oblation; but there was neither voice, nor any to answer, nor any that regarded.

units.leftText: Then Elijah said to all the people, “Come near to me.” So all the people approached him, and he repaired the altar of the LORD that had been torn down.
units.rightText: And Elijah said unto all the people, Come near unto me; and all the people came near unto him. And he repaired the altar of Jehovah that was thrown down.

units.leftText: And Elijah took twelve stones, one for each tribe of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of the LORD had come and said, “Israel shall be your name.”
units.rightText: And Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, unto whom the word of Jehovah came, saying, Israel shall be thy name.

units.leftText: And with the stones, Elijah built an altar in the name of the LORD. Then he dug a trench around the altar large enough to hold two seahs of seed.
units.rightText: And with the stones he built an altar in the name of Jehovah; and he made a trench about the altar, as great as would contain two measures of seed.
leftNotes: 18:32 2 seahs is approximately 13.2 dry quarts or 14.6 liters (probably about 25.4 pounds or 11.5 kilograms of seed).

units.leftText: Next, he arranged the wood, cut up the bull, placed it on the wood,
units.rightText: And he put the wood in order, and cut the bullock in pieces, and laid it on the wood. And he said, Fill four jars with water, and pour it on the burnt-offering, and on the wood.

units.leftText: and said, “Fill four waterpots and pour the water on the offering and on the wood.” “Do it a second time,” he said, and they did it a second time. “Do it a third time,” he said, and they did it a third time.
units.rightText: And he said, Do it the second time; and they did it the second time. And he said, Do it the third time; and they did it the third time.
leftNotes: 18:34 Some texts continue verse 33 to this point.

units.leftText: So the water ran down around the altar and even filled the trench. Elijah’s Prayer
units.rightText: And the water ran round about the altar; and he filled the trench also with water.

units.leftText: At the time of the evening sacrifice, Elijah the prophet approached the altar and said, “O LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known this day that You are God in Israel and that I am Your servant and have done all these things at Your command.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at the time of the offering of the evening oblation, that Elijah the prophet came near, and said, O Jehovah, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known this day that thou art God in Israel, and that I am thy servant, and that I have done all these things at thy word.

units.leftText: Answer me, O LORD! Answer me, so that this people will know that You, the LORD, are God, and that You have turned their hearts back again.”
units.rightText: Hear me, O Jehovah, hear me, that this people may know that thou, Jehovah, art God, and that thou hast turned their heart back again.

units.leftText: Then the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, and the dust, and it licked up the water in the trench.
units.rightText: Then the fire of Jehovah fell, and consumed the burnt-offering, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench.

units.leftText: When all the people saw this, they fell facedown and said, “The LORD, He is God! The LORD, He is God!”
units.rightText: And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces: and they said, Jehovah, he is God; Jehovah, he is God.

units.leftText: Then Elijah ordered them, “Seize the prophets of Baal! Do not let a single one escape.” So they seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the Kishon Valley and slaughtered them there. The LORD Sends Rain
units.rightText: And Elijah said unto them, Take the prophets of Baal; let not one of them escape. And they took them; and Elijah brought them down to the brook Kishon, and slew them there.

units.leftText: And Elijah said to Ahab, “Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of a heavy rain.”
units.rightText: And Elijah said unto Ahab, Get thee up, eat and drink; for there is the sound of abundance of rain.

units.leftText: So Ahab went up to eat and drink. But Elijah climbed to the summit of Carmel, bent down on the ground, and put his face between his knees.
units.rightText: So Ahab went up to eat and to drink. And Elijah went up to the top of Carmel; and he bowed himself down upon the earth, and put his face between his knees.

units.leftText: “Go and look toward the sea,” he said to his servant. So the servant went and looked, and he said, “There is nothing there.” Seven times Elijah said, “Go back.”
units.rightText: And he said to his servant, Go up now, look toward the sea. And he went up, and looked, and said, There is nothing. And he said, Go again seven times.

units.leftText: On the seventh time the servant reported, “There is a cloud as small as a man’s hand rising from the sea.” And Elijah replied, “Go and tell Ahab, ‘Prepare your chariot and go down before the rain stops you.’”
units.rightText: And it came to pass at the seventh time, that he said, Behold, there ariseth a cloud out of the sea, as small as a man’s hand. And he said, Go up, say unto Ahab, Make ready thy chariot, and get thee down, that the rain stop thee not.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, the sky grew dark with clouds and wind, and a heavy rain began to fall. So Ahab rode away and went to Jezreel.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in a little while, that the heavens grew black with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain. And Ahab rode, and went to Jezreel:

units.leftText: And the hand of the LORD came upon Elijah, and he tucked his cloak into his belt and ran ahead of Ahab all the way to Jezreel.
units.rightText: and the hand of Jehovah was on Elijah; and he girded up his loins, and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.
leftNotes: 18:46 Hebrew he girded up his loins

units.leftText: Now Ahab told Jezebel everything that Elijah had done and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
units.rightText: And Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and withal how he had slain all the prophets with the sword.

units.leftText: So Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, “May the gods deal with me, and ever so severely, if by this time tomorrow I have not made your life like the lives of those you killed!”
units.rightText: Then Jezebel sent a messenger unto Elijah, saying, So let the gods do to me, and more also, if I make not thy life as the life of one of them by to-morrow about this time.

units.leftText: And Elijah was afraid and ran for his life. When he came to Beersheba in Judah, he left his servant there,
units.rightText: And when he saw that, he arose, and went for his life, and came to Beer-sheba, which belongeth to Judah, and left his servant there.

units.leftText: while he himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness. He sat down under a broom tree and prayed that he might die. “I have had enough, LORD,” he said. “Take my life, for I am no better than my fathers.”
units.rightText: But he himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness, and came and sat down under a juniper-tree: and he requested for himself that he might die, and said, It is enough; now, O Jehovah, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers.

units.leftText: Then he lay down under the broom tree and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel touched him and said, “Get up and eat.”
units.rightText: And he lay down and slept under a juniper-tree; and, behold, an angel touched him, and said unto him, Arise and eat.

units.leftText: And he looked around, and there by his head was a cake of bread baked over hot coals, and a jar of water. So he ate and drank and lay down again.
units.rightText: And he looked, and, behold, there was at his head a cake baken on the coals, and a cruse of water. And he did eat and drink, and laid him down again.

units.leftText: A second time the angel of the LORD returned and touched him, saying, “Get up and eat, or the journey will be too much for you.”
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah came again the second time, and touched him, and said, Arise and eat, because the journey is too great for thee.

units.leftText: So he got up and ate and drank. And strengthened by that food, he walked forty days and forty nights until he reached Horeb, the mountain of God. The LORD Speaks to Elijah at Horeb
units.rightText: And he arose, and did eat and drink, and went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights unto Horeb the mount of God.
leftNotes: 19:8 That is, Mount Sinai, or possibly a mountain in the range containing Mount Sinai

units.leftText: There Elijah entered a cave and spent the night. And the word of the LORD came to him, saying, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”
units.rightText: And he came thither unto a cave, and lodged there; and, behold, the word of Jehovah came to him, and he said unto him, What doest thou here, Elijah?

units.leftText: “I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of Hosts,” he replied, “but the Israelites have forsaken Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and killed Your prophets with the sword. I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well.”
units.rightText: And he said, I have been very jealous for Jehovah, the God of hosts; for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword: and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away.
leftNotes: 19:10 Cited in Romans 11:3|ROM 11:3*; here and in verse 14

units.leftText: Then the LORD said, “Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD. Behold, the LORD is about to pass by.” And a great and mighty wind tore into the mountains and shattered the rocks before the LORD, but the LORD was not in the wind. After the wind there was an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake.
units.rightText: And he said, Go forth, and stand upon the mount before Jehovah. And, behold, Jehovah passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before Jehovah; but Jehovah was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but Jehovah was not in the earthquake:

units.leftText: After the earthquake there was a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire.
units.rightText: and after the earthquake a fire; but Jehovah was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.

units.leftText: When Elijah heard it, he wrapped his face in his cloak and went out and stood at the mouth of the cave. Suddenly a voice came to him and said, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”
units.rightText: And it was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out, and stood in the entrance of the cave. And, behold, there came a voice unto him, and said, What doest thou here, Elijah?

units.leftText: “I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of Hosts,” he replied, “but the Israelites have forsaken Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and killed Your prophets with the sword. I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well.”
units.rightText: And he said, I have been very jealous for Jehovah, the God of hosts; for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to him, “Go back by the way you came, and go to the Desert of Damascus. When you arrive, you are to anoint Hazael as king over Aram.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto him, Go, return on thy way to the wilderness of Damascus: and when thou comest, thou shalt anoint Hazael to be king over Syria;

units.leftText: You are also to anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king over Israel and Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel-meholah to succeed you as prophet.
units.rightText: and Jehu the son of Nimshi shalt thou anoint to be king over Israel; and Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah shalt thou anoint to be prophet in thy room.
leftNotes: 19:16 Or grandson; see 2 Kings 9:14|2KI 9:14*.
